   53  \section{Reduction to contrast coordinates}\label{sec:red}
   54  
   55  Let $U\in\R^{n\times N}$ with $U\tr U=I_N$ and $UU\tr=C$. Put
   56  \[
   57  X_c:=U\tr X\in\R^{N\times p},\qquad y_c:=U\tr y^r\in\R^N,\qquad e:=U\tr\varepsilon,\qquad \mu_c:=X_c\theta^\star .
   58  \]
   59  For $S\subseteq[p]$ let $X_{c,S}$ be the columns of $X_c$ in $S$, $P_S$ the orthogonal projection of $\R^N$ onto $\operatorname{col}(X_{c,S})$ ($P_\emptyset=0$), and
   60  \[
   61  M_S:=n\,X_{c,S}H_S^{-1}X_{c,S}\tr\ (M_\emptyset=0),\qquad t_S:=y_c\tr M_Sy_c,\qquad Q^c_S:=\|y_c\|^2-t_S,\qquad b:=b_0s_y^2 .
   62  \]
   63  
   64  \begin{lemma}[reduction]\label{lem:red}
   65  For every valid input:
   66  \begin{enumerate}
   67  \item[(a)] $G_S=X_{c,S}\tr X_{c,S}$, $s_yz_S=X_{c,S}\tr y_c$, $\|y_c\|^2=Ns_y^2$ and $s_y^2Q_S=Q^c_S\ge0$. Consequently, for all $S,T\subseteq[p]$,
   68  \begin{equation}\label{eq:score}
   69  \log\frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(T)}=\log\frac{w(|S|)}{w(|T|)}-\frac12\log\frac{D_S}{D_T}-\nu\log\frac{2b+Q^c_S}{2b+Q^c_T}.
   70  \end{equation}
   71  \item[(b)] $y_c=\mu_c+e$ and, under G, $e\sim N_N(0,\sst I_N)$. Moreover $\|\mu_c\|=\|\mu\|$, and $\mu_c\in\operatorname{col}(X_{c,S_0})$, so $(I-P_S)\mu_c=0$ whenever $S\supseteq S_0$.
   72  \end{enumerate}
   73  \end{lemma}
   74  
   75  \begin{proof}
   76  (a) $C$ is a symmetric idempotent and $X=CX^rD_x^{-1}$, so $CX=X$. Hence $X_c\tr X_c=X\tr UU\tr X=X\tr CX=X\tr X$, which gives the first identity. Next $s_yz_S=X_S\tr Cy^r=X_S\tr UU\tr y^r=X_{c,S}\tr y_c$, and $\|y_c\|^2=(y^r)\tr UU\tr y^r=(y^r)\tr Cy^r=Ns_y^2$, which also equals $s_y^2\,y\tr y$. Therefore $s_y^2Q_S=\|y_c\|^2-n(s_yz_S)\tr H_S^{-1}(s_yz_S)=Q^c_S$. Nonnegativity: by Lemma~\ref{lem:smoother}(b) below, $M_S\preceq P_S\preceq I$. Since $2b_0+Q_S=s_y^{-2}(2b+Q^c_S)$,
   77  \[
   78  \log m(S)=\log\frac{(2b_0)^{a_0}\Gamma(\nu)}{\pi^{n/2}\Gamma(a_0)}+\nu\log s_y^2-\frac12\log D_S-\nu\log(2b+Q^c_S),
   79  \]
   80  and the first two terms do not depend on $S$. This gives \eqref{eq:score}.
   81  
   82  (b) $\|U\tr\1\|^2=\1\tr C\1=0$, so $U\tr\1=0$. Also $U\tr C=U\tr UU\tr=U\tr$ and $CX^r=XD_x$, so $U\tr X^r\beta^\star=U\tr CX^r\beta^\star=U\tr XD_x\beta^\star=X_c\theta^\star$. Hence $y_c=U\tr(\alpha^\star\1+X^r\beta^\star+\varepsilon)=\mu_c+e$, and $e=U\tr\varepsilon\sim N_N(0,\sst U\tr U)=N_N(0,\sst I_N)$ under G. Further $\|\mu_c\|^2=\theta^{\star\top}X\tr CX\theta^\star=\|X\theta^\star\|^2=\|\mu\|^2$, and $\mu_c=X_{c,S_0}\theta^\star_{S_0}$ since $\operatorname{supp}\theta^\star=\operatorname{supp}\beta^\star=S_0$ ($D_x$ is diagonal with positive entries).
   83  \end{proof}
   84  
   85  Under G the set of $\varepsilon$ for which $y^r$ is constant has probability zero ($n\ge2$, $\sst>0$), so $\pi$ is $\Pp$-almost surely defined; it is a measurable function of $\varepsilon$. From now on everything is expressed through $(X_c,y_c,e,\mu_c)$, \eqref{eq:score} and \eqref{eq:ratio}. The design quantities $G_S,H_S,D_S,P_S,M_S$ are deterministic; $b$, $t_S$, $Q^c_S$ are random. Note that $b$ is the same for every model, so it never has to be integrated against; it only needs to be bounded (Lemma~\ref{lem:ongood}(a)).
   86  
   87  \section{Deterministic preliminaries}\label{sec:det}
   88  
   89  Write $h(\lambda)=n\lambda/((n+1)\lambda+1)$ for $\lambda\ge0$, and
   90  \[
   91  \eta_n:=\frac{1}{(n+1)N\vp}.
   92  \]
   93  
   94  \begin{lemma}[ridge smoother]\label{lem:smoother}
   95  Let $S\ne\emptyset$.
   96  \begin{enumerate}
   97  \item[(a)] $M_S=h(X_{c,S}X_{c,S}\tr)$ (functional calculus). Hence $M_S$ vanishes on $\operatorname{col}(X_{c,S})^\perp$, and on $\operatorname{col}(X_{c,S})$ its eigenvalues are $h(\lambda)$ for the nonzero eigenvalues $\lambda$ of $G_S$.
   98  \item[(b)] $0\preceq M_S\preceq\frac{n}{n+1}P_S\preceq P_S$.
   99  \item[(c)] If $\lambda_{\min}(G_S)\ge N\vp$, then $M_S\succeq(1-\eta_n)\frac n{n+1}P_S$.
  100  \item[(d)] If $S\subseteq T$ then $M_S\preceq M_T$; hence $t_S\le t_T$. (Also true for $S=\emptyset$.)
  101  \end{enumerate}
  102  \end{lemma}
  103  
  104  \begin{proof}
  105  (a) With $a=n+1$ and $Y=X_{c,S}$, $Y(aY\tr Y+I)=(aYY\tr+I)Y$, so $Y(aY\tr Y+I)^{-1}=(aYY\tr+I)^{-1}Y$ and $M_S=n(aYY\tr+I)^{-1}YY\tr=h(YY\tr)$, the two factors commuting. The nonzero eigenvalues of $YY\tr$ are those of $Y\tr Y=G_S$, and their eigenvectors span $\operatorname{col}(Y)$; $h(0)=0$.
  106  (b) $h$ is increasing with $0\le h<\frac n{n+1}$; apply (a).
  107  (c) On $\operatorname{col}(Y)$ every eigenvalue of $YY\tr$ is $\ge N\vp$, so by (a) and monotonicity $M_S\succeq h(N\vp)P_S$, and $h(g)=\frac n{n+1}\big(1-\frac1{(n+1)g+1}\big)\ge\frac n{n+1}\big(1-\frac1{(n+1)g}\big)$; take $g=N\vp$.
  108  (d) $h(\lambda)=\frac n{n+1}\big(1-((n+1)\lambda+1)^{-1}\big)$. If $0\preceq B_1\preceq B_2$, then $((n+1)B_2+I)^{-1}\preceq((n+1)B_1+I)^{-1}$, so $h(B_1)\preceq h(B_2)$. Apply this with $B_1=X_{c,S}X_{c,S}\tr=\sum_{i\in S}x_{c,i}x_{c,i}\tr\preceq X_{c,T}X_{c,T}\tr=B_2$. For $S=\emptyset$, $M_\emptyset=0\preceq M_T$ by (b).
  109  \end{proof}
  110  
  111  \begin{corollary}\label{cor:diff}
  112  Let $S\subseteq T$, $T\ne\emptyset$, $\lambda_{\min}(G_T)\ge N\vp$. Then for every $u\in\R^N$,
  113  \[
  114  \tfrac n{n+1}\big[\|(P_T-P_S)u\|^2-\eta_n\|P_Tu\|^2\big]\le u\tr(M_T-M_S)u\le\tfrac n{n+1}\big[\|(P_T-P_S)u\|^2+\eta_n\|P_Su\|^2\big].
  115  \]
  116  \end{corollary}
  117  
  118  \begin{proof}
  119  If $S\ne\emptyset$, Cauchy interlacing gives $\lambda_{\min}(G_S)\ge\lambda_{\min}(G_T)\ge N\vp$. Upper bound: $M_T\preceq\frac n{n+1}P_T$ and $M_S\succeq(1-\eta_n)\frac n{n+1}P_S$ (trivially true for $S=\emptyset$), so $M_T-M_S\preceq\frac n{n+1}(P_T-P_S)+\eta_n\frac n{n+1}P_S$. Lower bound: $M_T\succeq(1-\eta_n)\frac n{n+1}P_T$ and $M_S\preceq\frac n{n+1}P_S$. Finally $P_T-P_S$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{col}(X_{c,T})\ominus\operatorname{col}(X_{c,S})$, so $u\tr(P_T-P_S)u=\|(P_T-P_S)u\|^2$.
  120  \end{proof}
  121  
  122  \begin{lemma}[determinants]\label{lem:det}
  123  $1\le D_S\le(n+1)^{|S|}$ for every $S$. Let $S\subseteq T$ and $j=|T|-|S|$. Then $D_T/D_S\le(n+1)^j$, and if $\lambda_{\min}(G_T)\ge N\vp$ then $D_T/D_S\ge\big[(n+1)\big(1+\tfrac1{N\vp}\big)^{-1}\big]^j$.
  124  \end{lemma}
  125  
  126  \begin{proof}
  127  With $f(\lambda)=((n+1)\lambda+1)/(\lambda+1)$, increasing, $f(0)=1$, $f<n+1$, simultaneous diagonalisation gives $D_S=\prod_{i}f(\lambda_i(G_S))$, whence the first claim. Order eigenvalues increasingly; interlacing gives $\lambda_i(G_T)\le\lambda_i(G_S)\le\lambda_{i+j}(G_T)$, $1\le i\le|S|$. So $\prod_{i\le|S|}f(\lambda_i(G_T))\le D_S\le\prod_{i>j}f(\lambda_i(G_T))$. Dividing $D_T=\prod_{i\le|T|}f(\lambda_i(G_T))$ by these: $D_T/D_S\le\prod_{i>|S|}f(\lambda_i(G_T))\le(n+1)^j$ and $D_T/D_S\ge\prod_{i\le j}f(\lambda_i(G_T))\ge f(N\vp)^j$, with $f(g)\ge(n+1)g/(g+1)=(n+1)(1+1/g)^{-1}$.
  128  \end{proof}
  129  
  130  \begin{lemma}[prior ratios]\label{lem:prior}
  131  For $0\le k\le p-1$, $w(k+1)/w(k)=(k+1)/(2p-1-k)$. Hence:
  132  \begin{enumerate}
  133  \item[(a)] $w(k)/w(k')\le(2p)^{k'-k}$ for $0\le k<k'\le p$;
  134  \item[(b)] for $j\ge1$ with $s_0+j\le p$: $\binom{p-s_0}{j}\frac{w(s_0+j)}{w(s_0)}\le2\binom{s_0+j}{j}2^{-j}\le2(j+1)^{s_0}2^{-j}$.
  135  \end{enumerate}
  136  \end{lemma}
  137  
  138  \begin{proof}
  139  $w(k)=\frac12k!(2p-1-k)!/(2p-1)!$ gives the ratio. (a) $w(k)/w(k+1)=(2p-1-k)/(k+1)\le2p$. (b) Writing both factors as products over $i=0,\dots,j-1$,
  140  \[
  141  \binom{p-s_0}{j}\frac{w(s_0+j)}{w(s_0)}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}\frac{p-s_0-i}{i+1}\cdot\frac{s_0+i+1}{2p-s_0-i-1}=\binom{s_0+j}{j}\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}\frac{p-s_0-i}{2p-s_0-i-1}.
  142  \]
  143  The denominators are $\ge p$ since $i\le p-s_0-1$. Each factor is $\le\frac12$ when $s_0+i\ge1$ (as $2(p-s_0-i)\le2p-s_0-i-1$ iff $s_0+i\ge1$); the only other case is $s_0=i=0$, where the factor is $p/(2p-1)\le1$. So the product is $\le2\cdot2^{-j}$. Finally $\binom{s_0+j}{j}=\prod_{i=1}^{s_0}\frac{j+i}{i}\le(j+1)^{s_0}$.
  144  \end{proof}
  145  
  146  \begin{lemma}[signal left by an underfitting model]\label{lem:signal}
  147  Let $J=J(S)\ne\emptyset$ and $\lambda_{\min}(G_{S'})\ge N\vp$. Then $\Delta_S:=\|(I-P_S)\mu_c\|^2\ge N\vp\|\theta^\star_J\|^2$.
  148  \end{lemma}
  149  
  150  \begin{proof}
  151  $\mu_c=X_{c,S_0\cap S}\theta^\star_{S_0\cap S}+X_{c,J}\theta^\star_J$ and $(I-P_S)X_{c,S_0\cap S}=0$, so $\Delta_S=\min_{\gamma}\|X_{c,J}\theta^\star_J-X_{c,S}\gamma\|^2$. Since $S'=S\sqcup J$, each vector $X_{c,J}\theta^\star_J-X_{c,S}\gamma$ equals $X_{c,S'}\vartheta$ with $\vartheta=(\theta^\star_J,-\gamma)$, and $\|X_{c,S'}\vartheta\|^2\ge\lambda_{\min}(G_{S'})\|\vartheta\|^2\ge N\vp\|\theta^\star_J\|^2$.
  152  \end{proof}
  153  
  154  \begin{lemma}[chi-square facts]\label{lem:chi}
  155  Let $\chi^2_d$ be chi-square with $d\ge1$ degrees of freedom.
  156  \begin{enumerate}
  157  \item[(a)] For $x>0$: $P(\chi^2_d\ge d+2\sqrt{dx}+2x)\le e^{-x}$ and $P(\chi^2_d\le d-2\sqrt{dx})\le e^{-x}$; moreover $d+2\sqrt{dx}+2x\le2d+3x$. If $d\le d'$ then $P(\chi^2_d\ge t)\le P(\chi^2_{d'}\ge t)$ for all $t$.
  158  \item[(b)] For $\tau>0$: $E\big[e^{\chi^2_d/2}\1\{\chi^2_d\le\tau\}\big]=\dfrac{(\tau/2)^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)}\le\Big(\dfrac{e\tau}{d}\Big)^{d/2}$.
  159  \end{enumerate}
  160  \end{lemma}
  161  
  162  \begin{proof}
  163  (a) (Standard bounds; proved here in full, so no citation is relied on.) For $0<\lambda<\frac12$, $\log Ee^{\lambda(\chi^2_d-d)}=d\big(-\lambda-\frac12\log(1-2\lambda)\big)\le d\lambda^2/(1-2\lambda)$, because $-\log(1-u)-u=\sum_{k\ge2}u^k/k\le\frac{u^2}2\sum_{k\ge0}u^k=\frac{u^2}{2(1-u)}$ with $u=2\lambda$. Put $a=\sqrt d$, $s=\sqrt x$, $t=2as+2s^2$ and $\lambda=s/(a+2s)\in(0,\frac12)$; then $1-2\lambda=a/(a+2s)$, $d\lambda^2/(1-2\lambda)=as^2/(a+2s)$ and $\lambda t=2s^2(a+s)/(a+2s)$, so Chernoff's bound gives $P(\chi^2_d-d\ge t)\le\exp\{(as^2-2s^2(a+s))/(a+2s)\}=e^{-s^2}=e^{-x}$. For the lower tail, $\log Ee^{-\lambda(\chi^2_d-d)}=d\big(\lambda-\frac12\log(1+2\lambda)\big)\le d\lambda^2$ for $\lambda>0$ (as $\log(1+u)\ge u-u^2/2$ for $u\ge0$), so $P(d-\chi^2_d\ge t)\le e^{-\lambda t+d\lambda^2}=e^{-t^2/(4d)}$ at $\lambda=t/(2d)$; take $t=2\sqrt{dx}$. Next $2\sqrt{dx}\le d+x$. Finally $\chi^2_{d'}$ has the law of $\chi^2_d$ plus an independent nonnegative variable.
  164  
  165  (b) The density of $\chi^2_d$ is $x^{d/2-1}e^{-x/2}/(2^{d/2}\Gamma(d/2))$, so the truncated moment is
  166  \[\int_0^\tau x^{d/2-1}dx\big/\big(2^{d/2}\Gamma(d/2)\big)=\tau^{d/2}\big/\big(2^{d/2}\tfrac d2\Gamma(\tfrac d2)\big).\] And $\Gamma(z+1)\ge\int_z^\infty t^ze^{-t}dt\ge z^ze^{-z}$ for $z>0$.
  167  \end{proof}
  168  
  169  \section{The good event}\label{sec:good}
  170  
  171  For $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $1\le|J|\le m_n$ and $s_0+|J|\le p$ put $\chi^2_J:=\sigma_\star^{-2}\|(P_{S_0\cup J}-P_{S_0})e\|^2$. For an underfitting $S$ with $|S|\le m_n$ put $N_S:=\|(P_{S'}-P_S)e\|^2$ and $V_S:=\|(P_{S'}-P_S)y_c\|^2$. Under SE every $T\subseteq[p]$ with $1\le|T|\le m_n+s_0$ has $\lambda_{\min}(G_T)\ge N\vp>0$ (if $m_n+s_0>p$ this covers every nonempty $T$), so $X_{c,T}$ has full column rank; in particular $P_{S_0\cup J}-P_{S_0}$ is an orthogonal projection of rank $|J|$ and $\chi^2_J$ is exactly $\chi^2_{|J|}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:red}(b)), while $\sigma_\star^{-2}N_S$ is $\chi^2_{|J(S)|}$ with $|J(S)|\le s_0$.
  172  
  173  \begin{definition}
  174  $\Gn$ is the intersection of:
  175  \begin{itemize}
  176  \item[(G1)] $\big|\|e\|^2-N\sst\big|\le3\sst\sqrt{N\log n}$;
  177  \item[(G2)] $\|P_Te\|^2\le\sst C_A(m_n+s_0)\log n$ for every $T\subseteq[p]$ with $1\le|T|\le m_n+s_0$;
  178  \item[(G3)] $\chi^2_J\le\tau_{|J|}$ for every $J$ as above;
  179  \item[(G4)] $N_S\le\sst C_*\log n$ for every underfitting $S$ with $|S|\le m_n$ and $|J'(S)|\le j_*$.
  180  \end{itemize}
  181  \end{definition}
  182  
  183  \begin{lemma}\label{lem:Gprob}
  184  Under G, R and SE, $\Pp(\Gn^c)\le5/n$ for $n\ge n_0$.
  185  \end{lemma}
  186  
  187  \begin{proof}
  188  (G1) Lemma~\ref{lem:chi}(a) with $d=N$, $x=\log n$: outside probability $2/n$, $N-2\sqrt{N\log n}\le\|e\|^2/\sst\le N+2\sqrt{N\log n}+2\log n$, and $2\log n\le\sqrt{N\log n}$ once $N\ge4\log n$.
  189  
  190  (G2) For $|T|=k\ge1$, $\|P_Te\|^2/\sst$ is $\chi^2_{\operatorname{rank}}$ with rank $\le k$. There are at most $\binom pk\le p^k$ such $T$. With $x_k=k(\log p+1)+\log n$, Lemma~\ref{lem:chi}(a) and a union bound give exceptional probability $\le p^ke^{-x_k}=e^{-k}/n$; summing over $k\ge1$ gives $\le1/n$. On the complement, $\|P_Te\|^2/\sst\le2k+3x_k=5k+3k\log p+3\log n\le(5+3A+3)k\log n=C_Ak\log n$, using $\log p\le A\log n$, $\log n\ge1$, $k\ge1$; and $k\le m_n+s_0$.
  191  
  192  (G3) The same computation for the at most $p^j$ variables $\chi^2_J$ with $|J|=j$, each exactly $\chi^2_j$: exceptional probability $\le1/n$, threshold $C_Aj\log n=\tau_j$.
  193  
  194  (G4) An underfitting $S$ with $|J'(S)|\le j_*$ is determined by $J'(S)$ (at most $\sum_{j'\le j_*}\binom p{j'}\le(j_*+1)p^{j_*}$ choices) and $J(S)$ (a nonempty subset of $S_0$, fewer than $2^{s_0}$ choices). Each $N_S/\sst$ is stochastically at most $\chi^2_{s_0}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:chi}(a), last claim; if $s_0=0$ there is no underfitting model). With $x=j_*\log p+s_0\log2+\log(j_*+1)+\log n$, the union bound gives exceptional probability $\le1/n$, and on the complement $N_S/\sst\le2s_0+3x\le\big(2s_0+3[Aj_*+s_0+\log(j_*+1)+1]\big)\log n=C_*\log n$, using $\log p\le A\log n$ and $1,\log 2\le\log n$.
  195  \end{proof}
  196  
  197  Define the deterministic sequences
  198  \[
  199  \delta_n:=3\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{N}}+\frac{C_A(m_n+s_0)\log n}{N},\quad
  200  \delta''_n:=3\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{N}}+\frac{(12b_0+8)(M+\sst)}{N\sst},\quad
  201  \rho_n:=\frac{8(M+\sst)}{N\vp\sst}.
  202  \]
  203  By \eqref{eq:mn}, $\delta_n\log n\to0$, $\delta''_n\to0$, $\rho_n\to0$.
  204  
  205  \begin{lemma}[consequences of $\Gn$]\label{lem:ongood}
  206  Assume G, R, SE. For $n\ge n_0$, on $\Gn$:
  207  \begin{enumerate}
  208  \item[(a)] $\|y_c\|^2\le4n(M+\sst)$, and $0<b\le6b_0(M+\sst)$.
  209  \item[(b)] $\delta_n\le\frac12$, and $Q^c_S\ge N\sst(1-\delta_n)$ for every $S\supseteq S_0$ with $|S|\le m_n+s_0$.
  210  \item[(c)] For every underfitting $S$ with $|S|\le m_n$: $2b+Q^c_S\le E_n+V_S$, where $E_n:=2b+\|e\|^2+\frac2{n+1}\|y_c\|^2$ satisfies $N\sst(1-\delta_n)\le E_n\le N\sst(1+\delta''_n)$.
  211  \item[(d)] If $B\ge N\sst(1-\delta_n)$, then $\nu\frac n{n+1}\frac{\eta_n\|y_c\|^2}{B}\le\rho_n$.
  212  \end{enumerate}
  213  \end{lemma}
  214  
  215  \begin{proof}
  216  (a) $\|y_c\|^2\le2\|\mu_c\|^2+2\|e\|^2\le2nM+2N\sst(1+3\sqrt{\log n/N})\le4n(M+\sst)$ once $3\sqrt{\log n/N}\le1$, by R, Lemma~\ref{lem:red}(b) and (G1). Then $b=b_0\|y_c\|^2/N\le4b_0(M+\sst)n/(n-1)\le6b_0(M+\sst)$; $b>0$ because $s_y>0$.
  217  
  218  (b) $\delta_n\le\frac12$ for $n\ge n_0$ since $\delta_n\to0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:smoother}(b), $Q^c_S=y_c\tr(I-M_S)y_c\ge y_c\tr(I-P_S)y_c=\|(I-P_S)e\|^2=\|e\|^2-\|P_Se\|^2$, using $(I-P_S)\mu_c=0$. By (G1)--(G2) (for $S=\emptyset$, $\|P_\emptyset e\|=0$) this is $\ge N\sst-3\sst\sqrt{N\log n}-\sst C_A(m_n+s_0)\log n=N\sst(1-\delta_n)$.
  219  
  220  (c) If $S=\emptyset$, $Q^c_\emptyset=\|y_c\|^2=\|(I-P_\emptyset)y_c\|^2$. If $S\ne\emptyset$, SE gives $\lambda_{\min}(G_S)\ge N\vp$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:smoother}(c) gives $I-M_S\preceq(I-P_S)+\frac{1+n\eta_n}{n+1}P_S\preceq(I-P_S)+\frac2{n+1}P_S$ once $N\vp\ge1$ (then $n\eta_n\le1$). In both cases $Q^c_S\le\|(I-P_S)y_c\|^2+\frac2{n+1}\|y_c\|^2$. As $\operatorname{col}(X_{c,S})\subseteq\operatorname{col}(X_{c,S'})$, $\|(I-P_S)y_c\|^2=\|(I-P_{S'})y_c\|^2+V_S$, and $(I-P_{S'})y_c=(I-P_{S'})e$ because $S'\supseteq S_0$; so $\|(I-P_S)y_c\|^2\le\|e\|^2+V_S$. This gives the first claim. For the bounds on $E_n$: $E_n\ge\|e\|^2\ge N\sst(1-3\sqrt{\log n/N})\ge N\sst(1-\delta_n)$ by (G1); and by (a) and (G1), $E_n\le12b_0(M+\sst)+N\sst(1+3\sqrt{\log n/N})+8(M+\sst)=N\sst(1+\delta''_n)$.
  221  
  222  (d) $\nu=a_0+n/2\le n$, $\eta_n\|y_c\|^2\le4n(M+\sst)/((n+1)N\vp)$ by (a), and $B\ge N\sst/2$. So the left side is at most $8n^3(M+\sst)/((n+1)^2N^2\vp\sst)\le\rho_n$, because $n^3\le(n+1)^2(n-1)$ (equivalent to $n^2-n-1\ge0$).
  223  \end{proof}
  224  
  225  \section{Supersets of size at most \texorpdfstring{$m_n$}{m\_n}}\label{sec:sup}
  226  
  227  For $j\ge1$ let $\Xi_j:=\sum_{J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0,\,|J|=j}\ell(S_0\cup J)/\ell(S_0)$ ($\Xi_j=0$ if $s_0+j>p$). By \eqref{eq:ratio}, since every superset $S\in\Omega$ with $|S|\le m_n$ is $S_0\cup J$ with $1\le|J|\le m_n$,
  228  \begin{equation}\label{eq:supsum}
  229  \Pi(\{S\supsetneq S_0,\ |S|\le m_n\}\mid y)\le\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}\Xi_j .
  230  \end{equation}
  231  
  232  \begin{lemma}[one superset]\label{lem:onesup}
  233  Assume G, R, SE; $n\ge n_0$. On $\Gn$, for every $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $1\le|J|=j\le m_n$ and $S=S_0\cup J$,
  234  \[
  235  \frac{m(S)}{m(S_0)}\le(n+1)^{-j/2}\Big(1+\frac1{N\vp}\Big)^{j/2}\exp\Big\{\frac{\upsilon_n}2\chi^2_J+\rho_n\Big\},\qquad
  236  \upsilon_n:=\frac{1+(0.02n+1)/(n^2-1)}{1-\delta_n}.
  237  \]
  238  Moreover $1\le\upsilon_n$, $\upsilon_n-1\le2\big(\delta_n+(0.02n+1)/(n^2-1)\big)$, and $\epsilon_n:=(\upsilon_n-1)C_A\log n/2\to0$.
  239  \end{lemma}
  240  
  241  \begin{proof}
  242  By \eqref{eq:score} (with equal prior weights removed), exactly
  243  \[
  244  \frac{m(S)}{m(S_0)}=\Big(\frac{D_{S_0}}{D_S}\Big)^{1/2}\Big(1+\frac{t_S-t_{S_0}}{2b+Q^c_S}\Big)^{\nu}.
  245  \]
  246  \emph{Determinant.} $|S|=s_0+j\le m_n+s_0$, so SE and Lemma~\ref{lem:det} give $(D_{S_0}/D_S)^{1/2}\le(n+1)^{-j/2}(1+1/(N\vp))^{j/2}$.
  247  \emph{Numerator.} $t_S-t_{S_0}\ge0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:smoother}(d)); Corollary~\ref{cor:diff} with $(S,T)=(S_0,S)$ and $u=y_c$, together with $(P_S-P_{S_0})\mu_c=0$ (both projections fix $\mu_c$), gives $t_S-t_{S_0}\le\frac n{n+1}[\sst\chi^2_J+\eta_n\|y_c\|^2]$.
  248  \emph{Denominator.} $2b+Q^c_S\ge Q^c_S\ge N\sst(1-\delta_n)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:ongood}(b).
  249  With $\log(1+x)\le x$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:ongood}(d) (with $B=2b+Q^c_S$),
  250  \[
  251  \nu\log\Big(1+\frac{t_S-t_{S_0}}{2b+Q^c_S}\Big)\le\frac{\nu n}{(n+1)N(1-\delta_n)}\chi^2_J+\rho_n ,
  252  \]
  253  and $\frac{\nu n}{(n+1)N}=\frac{(0.01+n/2)n}{n^2-1}=\frac12\big(1+\frac{0.02n+1}{n^2-1}\big)$, so the first term is $\frac{\upsilon_n}2\chi^2_J$. Finally $\upsilon_n\ge1$ is clear, $\upsilon_n-1=\frac{(0.02n+1)/(n^2-1)+\delta_n}{1-\delta_n}$ with $1-\delta_n\ge\frac12$, and $\epsilon_n\to0$ because $\delta_n\log n\to0$ and $\log n/n\to0$.
  254  \end{proof}
  255  
  256  \begin{proposition}[superset sums]\label{prop:sup}
  257  Assume G, R, SE. Define the nonnegative random variable
  258  \[
  259  \Upsilon_n:=\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}\ \sum_{\substack{J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0\\|J|=j}}\frac{w(s_0+j)}{w(s_0)}(n+1)^{-j/2}\Big(1+\frac1{N\vp}\Big)^{j/2}e^{j\epsilon_n}\,e^{\chi^2_J/2}\,\1\{\chi^2_J\le\tau_j\},
  260  \]
  261  and let $\Upsilon_n^{>j_1}$ be the part with $j>j_1$. Put
  262  \[
  263  q_n:=\Big[\frac{eC_A\log n}{4(n+1)}\Big(1+\frac1{N\vp}\Big)e^{2\epsilon_n}\Big]^{1/2},\qquad K_{s_0,j_1}:=\sum_{i\ge0}(j_1+2+i)^{s_0}2^{-i}.
  264  \]
  265  Then for $n\ge n_0$: (a) on $\Gn$, $\sum_{j=j_1+1}^{m_n}\Xi_j\le e^{\rho_n}\Upsilon_n^{>j_1}$ for every integer $j_1\ge0$; (b) $q_n\le\min\{\frac12,\sqrt{eC_A}\,r_n\}$ and $\E \Upsilon_n^{>j_1}\le2K_{s_0,j_1}q_n^{j_1+1}$; (c) $\Upsilon_n=O_{\Pp}(r_n)$ and $\sum_{j\le m_n}\Xi_j\1_{\Gn}=O_{\Pp}(r_n)$.
  266  \end{proposition}
  267  
  268  \begin{proof}
  269  (a) On $\Gn$, (G3) makes every indicator in $\Upsilon_n$ equal to one, and for $\chi^2_J\le\tau_j$, $e^{\upsilon_n\chi^2_J/2}\le e^{\chi^2_J/2}e^{(\upsilon_n-1)\tau_j/2}=e^{\chi^2_J/2}e^{j\epsilon_n}$ (as $\upsilon_n\ge1$). Insert into Lemma~\ref{lem:onesup}, multiply by $w(s_0+j)/w(s_0)$ and sum over $J$ and $j>j_1$.
  270  
  271  (b) $q_n^2=\frac{eC_A\log n}{n}\cdot\frac{n}{4(n+1)}(1+\frac1{N\vp})e^{2\epsilon_n}$ and the second factor tends to $\frac14$, so $q_n\le\sqrt{eC_A}r_n$ and $q_n\le\frac12$ for $n\ge n_0$. All weights in $\Upsilon_n$ are deterministic and each $\chi^2_J$ is exactly $\chi^2_j$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:chi}(b) each term has expectation at most the weight times $(e\tau_j/j)^{j/2}=(eC_A\log n)^{j/2}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:prior}(b),
  272  \[
  273  \E \Upsilon_n^{>j_1}\le\sum_{j>j_1}2(j+1)^{s_0}2^{-j}(n+1)^{-j/2}\Big(1+\frac1{N\vp}\Big)^{j/2}e^{j\epsilon_n}(eC_A\log n)^{j/2}=\sum_{j>j_1}2(j+1)^{s_0}q_n^j,
  274  \]
  275  and with $q_n\le\frac12$, $\sum_{j>j_1}(j+1)^{s_0}q_n^j=q_n^{j_1+1}\sum_{i\ge0}(j_1+2+i)^{s_0}q_n^i\le K_{s_0,j_1}q_n^{j_1+1}$.
  276  
  277  (c) By (b) with $j_1=0$ and Markov's inequality, $\Pp(\Upsilon_n>2LK_{s_0,0}q_n)\le1/L$ for all $L>0$, and $q_n\le\sqrt{eC_A}r_n$; so $\Upsilon_n=O_{\Pp}(r_n)$. By (a), $\sum_{j\le m_n}\Xi_j\1_{\Gn}\le e^{\rho_n}\Upsilon_n$ with $\rho_n\to0$.
  278  \end{proof}
  279  
  280  \section{Underfitting models of size at most \texorpdfstring{$m_n$}{m\_n}}\label{sec:under}
  281  
  282  Throughout, $S$ is underfitting with $|S|\le m_n$, $J=J(S)$, $J'=J'(S)$, $|S'|=|S|+|J|\le m_n+s_0$; so SE applies to $S$ (if nonempty) and to $S'$. The model $S$ need not lie in $\Omega$ for the bounds of this section.
  283  
  284  \begin{lemma}[$S$ against $S'$]\label{lem:SvsSp}
  285  Assume G, R, SE; $n\ge n_0$. On $\Gn$, for every such $S$,
  286  \[
  287  \begin{aligned}\frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(S')}&\le(2p)^{|J|}(n+1)^{|J|/2}\exp\Big\{-\nu\frac n{n+1}\frac{V_S}{E_n+V_S}+\rho_n\Big\}\\&\le(2p)^{|J|}(n+1)^{|J|/2}\exp\Big\{-\min\Big(\frac{V_S}{8\sst},\frac n5\Big)+\rho_n\Big\}.\end{aligned}
  288  \]
  289  In particular $\ell(S)/\ell(S')\le(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}e^{\rho_n}$.
  290  \end{lemma}
  291  
  292  \begin{proof}
  293  \emph{Prior.} $|S'|=|S|+|J|\le p$, so $w(|S|)/w(|S'|)\le(2p)^{|J|}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:prior}(a).
  294  \emph{Determinant.} $(D_{S'}/D_S)^{1/2}\le(n+1)^{|J|/2}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:det}.
  295  \emph{Variance factor.} By \eqref{eq:score} the remaining factor is $\big(\frac{2b+Q^c_{S'}}{2b+Q^c_S}\big)^\nu=(1-x)^\nu$ with $x:=\frac{t_{S'}-t_S}{2b+Q^c_S}$. Here $x\ge0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:smoother}(d), and $x<1$ since $2b+Q^c_{S'}>0$. So $(1-x)^\nu\le e^{-\nu x}$. By Corollary~\ref{cor:diff} (pair $S\subseteq S'$, $u=y_c$) and $\|P_{S'}y_c\|\le\|y_c\|$, $t_{S'}-t_S\ge\frac n{n+1}[V_S-\eta_n\|y_c\|^2]$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:ongood}(c), $0<2b+Q^c_S\le E_n+V_S$. Hence
  296  \[
  297  \nu x\ge\nu\frac n{n+1}\frac{V_S-\eta_n\|y_c\|^2}{E_n+V_S}\ge\nu\frac n{n+1}\frac{V_S}{E_n+V_S}-\nu\frac n{n+1}\frac{\eta_n\|y_c\|^2}{E_n}\ge\nu\frac n{n+1}\frac{V_S}{E_n+V_S}-\rho_n .
  298  \]
  299  (First step: if $V_S-\eta_n\|y_c\|^2\ge0$, enlarging the denominator decreases the quotient; otherwise the right side is negative while $\nu x\ge0$. Second step: $E_n+V_S\ge E_n>0$. Third: Lemma~\ref{lem:ongood}(c),(d) with $B=E_n$.) This is the first inequality.
  300  For the second, $\frac V{E_n+V}\ge\min(\frac V{2E_n},\frac12)$. With $\nu\ge n/2$, $E_n\le N\sst(1+\delta''_n)$ and $\delta''_n\le1$ ($n\ge n_0$): $\nu\frac n{n+1}\frac{V_S}{2E_n}\ge\frac{n^2}{n^2-1}\cdot\frac{V_S}{4\sst(1+\delta''_n)}\ge\frac{V_S}{8\sst}$, and $\nu\frac n{n+1}\cdot\frac12\ge\frac{n^2}{4(n+1)}\ge\frac n5$ for $n\ge4$. The last claim uses $V_S\ge0$, $|J|\le s_0$ and $2p,n+1\ge1$.
  301  \end{proof}
  302  
  303  \begin{lemma}[adding the signal]\label{lem:signalgain}
  304  Assume G, R, SE; $n\ge n_0$. On $\Gn$, if in addition $|J'(S)|\le j_*$ and $\Delta_S\ge L\sst\log n$ for some $L\ge4C_*$, then
  305  \[
  306  \frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(S')}\le\exp\Big\{s_0(A+1)\log n+\rho_n-\min\Big(\frac{L\log n}{32},\frac n5\Big)\Big\}.
  307  \]
  308  \end{lemma}
  309  
  310  \begin{proof}
  311  $P_{S'}\mu_c=\mu_c$, so $(P_{S'}-P_S)y_c=(I-P_S)\mu_c+(P_{S'}-P_S)e$ and $\sqrt{V_S}\ge\sqrt{\Delta_S}-\sqrt{N_S}$. By (G4), $N_S\le\sst C_*\log n\le\frac{C_*}L\Delta_S\le\frac14\Delta_S$, so $V_S\ge\frac14\Delta_S\ge\frac L4\sst\log n$ and $V_S/(8\sst)\ge L\log n/32$. For the prefactor: $|J|\le s_0$, $p\le n^A$, and $\log2+\frac12\log(n+1)\le\log n$ for $n\ge5$, so $(2p)^{|J|}(n+1)^{|J|/2}\le e^{s_0(A+1)\log n}$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:SvsSp}.
  312  \end{proof}
  313  
  314  \begin{lemma}[assembling the underfitting mass]\label{lem:assemble}
  315  Assume G, R, SE; $n\ge n_0$. Let $\Uc$ be a collection of underfitting models with $|S|\le m_n$ and
  316  \[
  317  \kappa_n(\Uc):=\max\Big\{\frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(S')}:S\in\Uc,\ |J'(S)|\le j_*\Big\}\quad(\max\emptyset:=0).
  318  \]
  319  On $\Gn$,
  320  \begin{equation}\label{eq:assemble}
  321  \sum_{S\in\Uc}\frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(S_0)}\le2^{s_0}\kappa_n(\Uc)\big(1+e^{\rho_n}\Upsilon_n\big)+2^{s_0}(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}e^{2\rho_n}\Upsilon_n^{>j_*},
  322  \end{equation}
  323  and $(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\Upsilon_n^{>j_*}=O_{\Pp}\big((\log n)^{(j_*+1)/2}/n\big)$.
  324  \end{lemma}
  325  
  326  \begin{proof}
  327  Write $\frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(S_0)}=\frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(S')}\cdot\frac{\ell(S')}{\ell(S_0)}$. A given $S'=S_0\cup J'$ arises from at most $2^{s_0}-1$ underfitting $S$, namely $S=J'\cup(S_0\setminus I)$ with $\emptyset\ne I\subseteq S_0$. Note $|J'(S)|\le|S|\le m_n$. For $|J'|\le j_*$ bound the first factor by $\kappa_n(\Uc)$; the second factor, summed over the distinct $S'$, is $1$ for $S'=S_0$ plus terms of $\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}\Xi_j\le e^{\rho_n}\Upsilon_n$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:sup}(a), $j_1=0$). For $|J'|>j_*$ bound the first factor by $(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}e^{\rho_n}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:SvsSp}) and the sum of the second over distinct $S'$ by $\sum_{j=j_*+1}^{m_n}\Xi_j\le e^{\rho_n}\Upsilon_n^{>j_*}$. This is \eqref{eq:assemble}.
  328  
  329  By Proposition~\ref{prop:sup}(b) and $q_n^2\le eC_A\log n/n$, $\E[(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\Upsilon_n^{>j_*}]\le2K_{s_0,j_*}2^{s_0}n^{As_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}(eC_A\log n)^{(j_*+1)/2}n^{-(j_*+1)/2}$. Since $j_*\ge(2A+1)s_0+1$, $\frac{j_*+1}2\ge s_0(A+\frac12)+1$, so $n^{As_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}n^{-(j_*+1)/2}\le(1+\frac1n)^{s_0/2}n^{-1}\le2^{s_0/2}n^{-1}$. Markov's inequality gives the $O_{\Pp}$ claim.
  330  \end{proof}

  332  \section{Proof of the theorem}\label{sec:main}
  333  
  334  In (i) and (iv), and in Steps 0--1, $n\ge n_0$; the deterministic parts of (ii) and (iii) hold for every $n$ (see there). Three elementary facts are used repeatedly. First, a finite sum of $O_{\Pp}(a_n)$ terms is $O_{\Pp}(a_n)$. Second, a bound valid for $n\ge n_0$, or of the form $\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_n\Pp(X_n>La_n)=0$, gives tightness of $X_n/a_n$ over all $n$, because for each fixed $n$ the single finite random variable $X_n/a_n$ is tight ($a_n>0$), and a finite family of tight variables is tight; for the posterior masses bounded below this is explicit, since they lie in $[0,1]$ and so $X_n/a_n\le1/a_n$. Third, if $Y_n\ge0$, $Y_n\1_{\Gn}=O_{\Pp}(a_n)$ and $\Pp(\Gn^c)\to0$, then $Y_n=O_{\Pp}(a_n)$, because $\Pp(Y_n>La_n)\le\Pp(Y_n\1_{\Gn}>La_n)+\Pp(\Gn^c)$. Also $n^{-2}\le n^{-1/2}\le r_n$ and $(\log n)^{(j_*+1)/2}/n=o(r_n)$.
  335  
  336  \paragraph{Step 0: the tail above $m_n$ (H-T02).} By H-T02 with $m=m_n$, and $2^{-m_n}\le(2p)^{-s_0}n^{-(s_0+1)/2}n^{-1/2}$ (definition of $m_n$),
  337  \begin{equation}\label{eq:tail}
  338  \Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)\le(2p)^{-s_0}n^{-(s_0+2)/2}(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\,\Theta_{n,m_n}=(1+\tfrac1n)^{s_0/2}n^{-1/2}\Theta_{n,m_n},
  339  \end{equation}
  340  and $\Pp(\Theta_{n,m_n}>L)\le\sup_m\Pp(\Theta_{n,m}>L)$, so $\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)=O_{\Pp}(n^{-1/2})$.
  341  
  342  \paragraph{Step 1: the signal under BM-C.} Let $\Uc$ be the set of underfitting $S\in\Omega$ with $|S|\le m_n$. For $S\in\Uc$, Lemma~\ref{lem:signal} (SE on $S'$) and BM-C give
  343  \[
  344  \Delta_S\ge N\vp\|\theta^\star_{J(S)}\|^2\ge N\vp\min_{j\in S_0}\theta^{\star2}_j\ge\Big(1-\frac1n\Big)M_*\sst\log n\ge L_*\sst\log n ,
  345  \]
  346  since $J(S)\ne\emptyset$ and $(1-\frac1n)(2L_*+1)\ge L_*$ for $n\ge2$. As $L_*\ge4C_*$, $L_*/32\ge s_0(A+1)+2$, and $n/5\ge(s_0(A+1)+2)\log n$ for $n\ge n_0$, Lemma~\ref{lem:signalgain} with $L=L_*$ gives on $\Gn$
  347  \begin{equation}\label{eq:kappa}
  348  \kappa_n(\Uc)\le\exp\{s_0(A+1)\log n+\rho_n-(s_0(A+1)+2)\log n\}=e^{\rho_n}n^{-2}.
  349  \end{equation}
  350  Under BM-$\infty$, $M_n\ge M_*$ for all large $n$, so BM-C holds for all large $n$; since the conclusions are asymptotic, BM-$\infty$ is covered by the BM-C case. (If $s_0=0$, $\Uc=\emptyset$ and Step 1 is void.)
  351  
  352  \paragraph{(i).} Every $S\in\Omega\setminus\{S_0\}$ either has $|S|>m_n$, or is a superset with $|S|\le m_n$, or lies in $\Uc$ (if $J(S)=\emptyset$ and $S\ne S_0$ then $J'(S)\ne\emptyset$). Hence
  353  \[
  354  1-\pi(S_0)\le\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)+\Pi(\{S\supsetneq S_0,|S|\le m_n\}\mid y)+\Pi(\Uc\mid y).
  355  \]
  356  The first term is $O_{\Pp}(n^{-1/2})$ by \eqref{eq:tail}. The second is at most $\sum_{j\le m_n}\Xi_j$ by \eqref{eq:supsum}, which is $O_{\Pp}(r_n)$ on $\Gn$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:sup}(c). By \eqref{eq:ratio}, \eqref{eq:assemble} and \eqref{eq:kappa}, on $\Gn$,
  357  \[
  358  \begin{aligned}\Pi(\Uc\mid y)\le\sum_{S\in\Uc}\frac{\ell(S)}{\ell(S_0)}&\le2^{s_0}e^{\rho_n}n^{-2}(1+e^{\rho_n}\Upsilon_n)+2^{s_0}e^{2\rho_n}(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\Upsilon_n^{>j_*}\\&=O_{\Pp}\Big(n^{-2}+\frac{(\log n)^{(j_*+1)/2}}{n}\Big),\end{aligned}
  359  \]
  360  using $\Upsilon_n=O_{\Pp}(r_n)$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:assemble}. Since $\Pp(\Gn^c)\le5/n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Gprob}), all three terms are $O_{\Pp}(r_n)$ without restriction to $\Gn$, and $1-\pi(S_0)=O_{\Pp}(r_n)$.
  361  
  362  \paragraph{(ii).} For $j\in S_0$, $1-\mathrm{PIP}_j=\pi(\{S:j\notin S\})\le\pi(\Omega\setminus\{S_0\})=1-\pi(S_0)$. For $j\notin S_0$, $\mathrm{PIP}_j=\pi(\{S:j\in S\})\le1-\pi(S_0)$. This uses only $S_0\in\Omega$, so it holds for every data set and every $n$ with $s_0\le K$; when $s_0>K$, $\pi(S_0):=0$ (reading 2 of \texttt{STATEMENT.md}) and the bound $|\mathrm{PIP}_j-\1\{j\in S_0\}|\le1$ is trivial. On the event $\{1-\pi(S_0)<\frac12\}$ it follows that $\mathrm{PIP}_j>\frac12$ exactly for $j\in S_0$, i.e.\ $\mathrm{MPM}=S_0$. By (i), $1-\pi(S_0)\to0$ in $\Pp$-probability, so $\Pp(\mathrm{MPM}=S_0)\ge\Pp(1-\pi(S_0)<\frac12)\to1$.
  363  
  364  \paragraph{(iii).} On $\{\pi(S_0)>\frac12\}$, every $S\in\Omega\setminus\{S_0\}$ has $\pi(S)\le1-\pi(S_0)<\frac12<\pi(S_0)$, i.e.\ $F(S)<F(S_0)$: $S_0$ is the strict global maximiser of $F$ on $\Omega$, so $S^\dagger=S_0$ and the tie rule is not invoked. Hence $\{S^\dagger\ne S_0\}\subseteq\{1-\pi(S_0)\ge\frac12\}$ and by Markov's inequality $\Pp(S^\dagger\ne S_0)\le2\E[1-\pi(S_0)]$. This argument holds for every $n$ with $s_0\le K$. (For the finitely many $n$ with $s_0>K$, $S_0\notin\Omega$, $\pi(S_0):=0$ and the bound reads $\Pp(S^\dagger\ne S_0)\le2$.) Finally, since $0\le1-\pi(S_0)\le1$, for every $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, $\E[1-\pi(S_0)]\le\epsilon+\Pp(1-\pi(S_0)>\epsilon)$, and the last probability tends to $0$ by (i); so $\limsup_n\E[1-\pi(S_0)]\le\epsilon$ for every $\epsilon$, i.e.\ $\E[1-\pi(S_0)]\to0$.
  365  
  366  \paragraph{(iv).} Here BM-C and BM-$\infty$ are not assumed. If $J_n=\emptyset$, then $\Pi(\{S\not\supseteq J_n\}\mid y)=0$ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, for $j\in J_n$ let $\Uc_j$ be the set of $S\in\Omega$ with $|S|\le m_n$ and $j\notin S$. Each $S\in\Uc_j$ is underfitting ($j\in J(S)$), and by Lemma~\ref{lem:signal} and the definition of $J_n$,
  367  \[
  368  \Delta_S\ge N\vp\|\theta^\star_{J(S)}\|^2\ge N\vp\theta^{\star2}_j\ge\Big(1-\frac1n\Big)M_*\sst\log n\ge L_*\sst\log n .
  369  \]
  370  No condition on the other coordinates of $\theta^\star$ is used: they are all fitted by $S'=S\cup S_0$. Exactly as in Step 1, $\kappa_n(\Uc_j)\le e^{\rho_n}n^{-2}$ on $\Gn$, and \eqref{eq:assemble} gives, on $\Gn$, a bound on $\Pi(\Uc_j\mid y)$ that does not depend on $j$:
  371  \[
  372  \Pi(\Uc_j\mid y)\le2^{s_0}e^{\rho_n}n^{-2}(1+e^{\rho_n}\Upsilon_n)+2^{s_0}e^{2\rho_n}(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\Upsilon_n^{>j_*}.
  373  \]
  374  Since $\{S\in\Omega:S\not\supseteq J_n\}\subseteq\{|S|>m_n\}\cup\bigcup_{j\in J_n}\Uc_j$ and $|J_n|\le s_0$,
  375  \[
  376  \begin{aligned}\Pi(\{S\not\supseteq J_n\}\mid y)&\le\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)+s_0\max_{j\in J_n}\Pi(\Uc_j\mid y)\\&=O_{\Pp}(n^{-1/2})+O_{\Pp}\Big(n^{-2}+\frac{(\log n)^{(j_*+1)/2}}n\Big)=O_{\Pp}(r_n),\end{aligned}
  377  \]
  378  by \eqref{eq:tail}, Lemma~\ref{lem:assemble} and Lemma~\ref{lem:Gprob}. For $j\in J_n$, $1-\mathrm{PIP}_j=\Pi(\{S:j\notin S\}\mid y)\le\Pi(\{S\not\supseteq J_n\}\mid y)$, so $1-\min_{j\in J_n}\mathrm{PIP}_j=O_{\Pp}(r_n)$ and $\min_{j\in J_n}\mathrm{PIP}_j\to1$ in $\Pp$-probability.
  379  
  380  \paragraph{(v).} If $s_0=0$, the minimum in BM-C and BM-$\infty$ is over the empty set, hence $+\infty$, and both conditions hold. For $c>0$, the BM-C inequality for $(\theta^\star/c,\sst/c^2)$ reads $\min_j\theta^{\star2}_j/c^2\ge M_*(\sst/c^2)\log n/(n\vp)$, which is the original inequality divided by $c^2$; $\varphi_0$ depends only on the standardised design and $M_*$, $n$ do not involve the scale. The same holds for BM-$\infty$ and for each defining inequality of $J_n$. This applies in particular to $c=s_y$. \qed
  381  
  382  \section{Remarks}
  383  
  384  \begin{remark}[on the constant $M_*$]
  385  BM-C enters only through Step 1 and (iv), via $(1-\frac1n)M_*\ge L_*$. The proof therefore gives (i)--(iv) with $M_*$ replaced by any constant $M$ with $M>L_*$ (then $(1-\frac1n)M\ge L_*$ for large $n$). This is a statement about this proof, not about sharpness; no lower bound on the needed signal is proved here.
  386  \end{remark}
  387  
  388  \begin{remark}[where the hypotheses enter]
  389  G gives the exact Gaussian law of $e$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:red}). R gives $p\le n^A$ (all union bounds and $j_*$), $\|\mu\|^2\le nM$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:ongood}) and $s_0\le K$ (so $S_0\in\Omega$). SE at sizes up to $m_n+s_0$ gives full rank and the eigenvalue bounds for $S$, $S'$ and $S_0\cup J$. H-T02 is used only in Step 0. The inverse-gamma rate $b=b_0s_y^2$ is random but common to all models; it enters only through $2b\ge0$ and the bound $b\le6b_0(M+\sst)$ on $\Gn$, so no change-of-rate argument is needed for the comparisons made here. The comparison of an underfitting $S$ with $S'=S\cup S_0$ (whose residual is pure noise) is what makes the beta-min scale $\sst$ rather than $\sst+M$.
  390  \end{remark}
  391  
  392  \begin{remark}[the cap]
  393  All comparisons are written with $\ell(S)=w(|S|)\,m(S)$, which is defined for every $S\subseteq[p]$; models $S'$ or $S_0\cup J$ outside $\Omega$ enter only as upper-bound devices, through nonnegative sums. The cap is used only to place $S_0$ in $\Omega$.
  394  \end{remark}
  395  
  396  \end{document}

The one unproved v3 result used is T02(i), as an explicit hypothesis (H-T02), as the brief allows (T03's file lists T01, T02 as "builds on").
    4  
    5  ## 1. Data and target (00_COMMON §1; METHODOLOGY_v3 §5)
    6  
    7  - Raw data $(X^r,y^r)$, $X^r\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, $n\ge3$, $p\ge1$, no constant column, $y^r$ not constant. $C=I_n-\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^\top/n$; $D_x$ = diagonal matrix of the raw column sample SDs (denominator $n-1$); $s_y^2=\|Cy^r\|^2/(n-1)$. Standardised data $X=CX^rD_x^{-1}$, $y=Cy^r/s_y$, so $\|x_j\|^2=\|y\|^2=n-1$. $U\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-1)}$ with $U^\top U=I_{n-1}$, $UU^\top=C$.
    8  - $K=\min(p,\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$, $\Omega=\{S\subseteq[p]:|S|\le K\}$. For $S\subseteq[p]$: $G_S=X_S^\top X_S$, $R_S=G_S/(n-1)$, $z_S=X_S^\top y$, $H_S=(n+1)G_S+I$, $D_S=\det H_S/\det(G_S+I)$, $Q_S=y^\top y-n z_S^\top H_S^{-1}z_S$; $a_0=b_0=0.01$, $\nu=a_0+n/2$ ($D_\emptyset=1$, $Q_\emptyset=y^\top y$).
    9  - $m(S)=\dfrac{(2b_0)^{a_0}\Gamma(\nu)}{\pi^{n/2}\Gamma(a_0)}D_S^{-1/2}(2b_0+Q_S)^{-\nu}$; $w(k)=\tfrac12\big/\binom{2p-1}{k}$ ($0\le k\le p$); $W_K=\sum_{k\le K}\binom pk w(k)$; $\varpi(S)=w(|S|)/W_K$ for $S\in\Omega$.
   10  - $F(S)=\log[\varpi(S)m(S)]$, $Z=\sum_{S\in\Omega}\varpi(S)m(S)$, $\pi(S)=e^{F(S)}/Z$ on $\Omega$; $\Pi(\mathcal A\mid y)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal A\cap\Omega}\pi(S)$.
   11  - $\mathrm{PIP}_j=\pi(\{S: j\in S\})$; $\mathrm{MPM}=\{j:\mathrm{PIP}_j>\tfrac12\}$; global HPM $S^\dagger=\arg\max_{\Omega}F$, ties broken by smallest size, then lexicographically.
   12  - Statistical model: $y^r=\alpha^\star\mathbf 1+X^r\beta^\star+\varepsilon$; $\mu=CX^r\beta^\star=X\theta^\star$ with $\theta^\star=D_x\beta^\star$; $S_0=\operatorname{supp}\beta^\star$, $s_0=|S_0|$. $P_0$, $E_0$ refer to $\varepsilon$ (the design is fixed).
   13  - $r_n=\sqrt{\log n/n}$. $m_n(\omega)=\lceil(s_0\log(2p)+(s_0+1)(\log n)/2+\omega)/\log2\rceil$, $m_n:=m_n(\tfrac12\log n)$.
   14  - Regime R1: $n\to\infty$, $s_0$ fixed, $p=p_n\le n^A$; design, $\beta^\star$, $S_0$ may vary with $n$.
   15  
   16  ## 2. Hypotheses
   17  
   18  - **G.** Fixed design; $\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,\sigma_\star^2I_n)$, $\sigma_\star^2>0$ fixed.
   19  - **R.** $s_0$ fixed; $p\le n^A$ with fixed $A\ge1$; $\|\mu\|^2/n\le M$ (fixed $M$); $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0})\ge\varphi_0^2>0$ (fixed $\varphi_0$); eventually $s_0\le K$.
   20  - **SE.** $\lambda_{\min}(R_T)\ge\varphi_0^2$ for every nonempty $T\subseteq[p]$ with $|T|\le\min(p,m_n+s_0)$.
   21  - **Constants.** $j_*=\lceil(2A+1)s_0\rceil+1$; $C_*=2s_0+3[Aj_*+s_0+\log(j_*+1)+1]$; $L_*=\max\{4C_*,\,32[s_0(A+1)+2]\}$; $M_*=2L_*+1$.
   22  - **BM-C.** $\min_{j\in S_0}\theta^{\star2}_j\ge M_*\sigma_\star^2\log n/(n\varphi_0^2)$.
   23  - **BM-∞.** The same inequality with a sequence $M_n\to\infty$ in place of $M_*$.
   24  - **H-T02 (= T02(i), unproved v3 conjecture, used as hypothesis).** Under G and R, for each deterministic integer sequence $m=m(n)$,
   25    $\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\le2^{-m}(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\,\Theta_{n,m}$, with $\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_n\sup_mP_0(\Theta_{n,m}>L)=0$.
   26  
   27  Convention: a minimum over the empty set is $+\infty$ (so BM-C and BM-∞ hold when $s_0=0$).
   28  
   29  ## 3. Conclusions (in R1)
   30  
   31  Under G, R, SE, H-T02 and BM-C (or BM-∞):
   32  
   33  - **(i)** $1-\pi(S_0)=O_{P_0}(r_n)$.
   34  - **(ii)** $\max_j|\mathrm{PIP}_j-\mathbf 1\{j\in S_0\}|\le1-\pi(S_0)$ for every data set (deterministic); and $P_0(\mathrm{MPM}=S_0)\to1$.
   35  - **(iii)** $P_0(S^\dagger\ne S_0)\le2E_0[1-\pi(S_0)]\to0$; on the event $\{\pi(S_0)>\tfrac12\}$, $S_0$ is the strict global maximiser of $F$ on $\Omega$ (the tie rule is not invoked).
   36  
   37  Under G, R, SE and H-T02 only (no beta-min):
   38  
   39  - **(iv)** With $J_n=\{j\in S_0:\theta^{\star2}_j\ge M_*\sigma_\star^2\log n/(n\varphi_0^2)\}$: $\Pi(\{S:S\not\supseteq J_n\}\mid y)=O_{P_0}(r_n)$, and $\min_{j\in J_n}\mathrm{PIP}_j\to1$ in $P_0$-probability (with $1-\min_{j\in J_n}\mathrm{PIP}_j=O_{P_0}(r_n)$; the minimum over $\emptyset$ is $1$).
   40  
   41  Deterministic remarks:
   42  
   43  - **(v)** If $s_0=0$, BM-C and BM-∞ hold vacuously. For every $c>0$, replacing $(\theta^\star,\sigma_\star^2)$ by $(\theta^\star/c,\sigma_\star^2/c^2)$ (in particular $c=s_y$) leaves the BM-C and BM-∞ inequalities and the set $J_n$ unchanged.
   44  
   45  ## 4. Not claimed
   46  
   47  The theorem file's sentences "No frequentist $O(r_n)$ selection-error rate follows from the posterior $O_{P_0}(r_n)$ rate" and "$M_*$ is conservative, not sharp; the sharp general-design constant is open" are interpretive remarks. They are not part of the claim and are not proved.
   48  
   49  ## 5. Readings adopted (not changes)
   50  
   51  1. $O_{P_0}(a_n)$ means $X_n/a_n$ is tight under $P_0$; "$\to$" for random quantities means convergence in $P_0$-probability.
   52  2. In (i)–(iii), $\pi(S_0)$ is defined once $s_0\le K$ (eventually, by R); before that, $\pi(S_0):=0$ and every claim holds trivially or is asymptotic.

   54  4. (v) is read as the scale invariance stated in §3; $\varphi_0$, $M_*$ and $n$ do not depend on the scale of $y$.

    5  **Category / rank:** consistency; **core** (theorem).
    6  
    7  ## Definitions used
    8  Target π, PIP_j, MPM, global HPM S† with the tie rule (00_COMMON §1); r_n; regime R1. Constants: j_* = ⌈(2A+1)s₀⌉ + 1; C_* = 2s₀ + 3[Aj_* + s₀ + log(j_*+1) + 1]; L_* = max{4C_*, 32[s₀(A+1)+2]}; M_* = 2L_* + 1.
    9  
   10  ## Assumptions
   11  G, R, SE (project); BM-C (new candidate fixed constant M_*; provisional, from the J1 audit of proofs/T7_T8 §5; the proving run may replace M_* by any constant it can justify) or BM-∞ (project; M_n → ∞), either suffices. No beta-min for the screening clause.
   12  
   13  ## Precise statement
   14  In R1 under G, R, SE and BM-C (or BM-∞):
   15  (i) 1 − π(S₀) = O_{P₀}(r_n).
   16  (ii) max_j |PIP_j − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ 1 − π(S₀) (deterministic given (i)); P₀(MPM = S₀) → 1.
   17  (iii) P₀(S† ≠ S₀) ≤ 2E₀[1 − π(S₀)] → 0; on {π(S₀) > ½}, S₀ is the strict global maximiser of F (the tie rule is not invoked).
   18  (iv) [screening; G, R, SE only] With J_n = {j ∈ S₀ : θ*_j² ≥ M_*σ*² log n/(nφ₀²)}: Π(S ⊉ J_n | y) = O_{P₀}(r_n); the PIPs of J_n tend uniformly to one. (Screening has its own underfitting comparison; it is not a consequence of full-support selection.)

    1  # W1-T03R — PROOF.md: exact BB(1,p) size tail, sharpened T02, restated T03
    2  
    3  Run W1-T03R, 2026-11-02. Notation of `Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md`. Status words are used per the campaign protocol and every status is a **candidate pending cross-family review**.
    4  
    5  **References to locked proofs (cited by label, unchanged unless said otherwise).**
    6  - **[P1]** `Docs/Theory/proofs/T01_T02_contrast_dimension/PROOF_v3.tex` (T01, T02). Labels used: `lem:spec`, `lem:prior`, `lem:chi`, `lem:num`, `lem:den`, `thm:T01iii`, `thm:Ta`, `thm:T02i`, `lem:good`, `lem:onG`, `lem:one`, `thm:T02ii`.
    7  - **[P3]** `Docs/Theory/proofs/T03_A2_selection_consistency/PROOF_v2.tex` (T03). Labels used: `lem:red`, `lem:smoother`, `cor:diff`, `lem:det`, `lem:prior`, `lem:signal`, `lem:chi`, `lem:Gprob`, `lem:ongood`, `lem:onesup`, `prop:sup`, `lem:SvsSp`, `lem:signalgain`, `lem:assemble`, "Step 0", "Step 1", paragraphs (i)–(v) of §"Proof of the theorem".
    8  
    9  Throughout: $N=n-1$, $K=\min(p,\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$, $w(k)=\tfrac12/\binom{2p-1}{k}$, $\varpi(S)=w(|S|)/W_K$, $r_n=\sqrt{\log n/n}$, $m_n(\omega)=\lceil(s_0\log(2p)+(s_0+1)(\log n)/2+\omega)/\log 2\rceil$ (00_COMMON). We assume $p\ge2$ (for $p=1$ every statement below is trivial or void).
   10  
   11  ---
   12  
   13  ## 1. The exact BB(1,p) size tail
   14  
   15  Put $q_k:=\binom pk w(k)$ ($0\le k\le p$) and, for every integer $m$ and $0\le s_0\le K$,
   16  $$R_m:=\frac{\varpi(\{S\in\Omega:|S|>m\})}{\varpi(S_0)}=\sum_{k=m+1}^{K}\frac{q_k}{w(s_0)}\qquad(\text{empty sum}=0;\ W_K\text{ cancels}).$$
   17  $R_m$ is a data-free number (it depends on $p$, $s_0$, $K$, $m$ only), and $R_m=0$ for $m\ge K$.
   18  
   19  ### Lemma E1 (exact tail; PROVED)
   20  Let $\rho_i:=\dfrac{p-i}{2p-1-i}$ for $0\le i\le p-1$.
   21  
   22  **(a)** $\rho_i=\tfrac12\Big(1-\dfrac{i-1}{2p-1-i}\Big)$, and for $s_0\le k\le p$: $\ q_k/w(s_0)=\binom p{s_0}\prod_{i=s_0}^{k-1}\rho_i$.
   23  
   24  **(b)** For every integer $m\ge s_0$:
   25  $$R_m\le\binom p{s_0}\,2^{-(m-s_0)}\,e^{-\gamma_m},\qquad \gamma_m:=\frac{m(m-1)-(s_0-1)(s_0-2)}{4(p-1)} .$$
   26  
   27  **(c)** If $s_0\ge1$ and $s_0\le m\le K-1$:
   28  $$R_m\ \ge\ \frac{q_{m+1}}{w(s_0)}\ \ge\ \binom p{s_0}\,2^{-(m+1-s_0)}\exp\Big\{-\frac{m(m-1)-(s_0-1)(s_0-2)}{4(p-m)}\Big\}.$$
   29  
   30  **(d)** (comparison with the locked bound) The locked proof of T02(i) bounds the same ratio by $4(2p)^{s_0}2^{-m}$ ([P1] `lem:prior`(c),(d)). For $m\ge s_0\ge 1$, (b) improves this by the factor at least $4\,s_0!\,e^{\gamma_m}$, since $\binom p{s_0}2^{s_0}\le(2p)^{s_0}/s_0!$.
   31  
   32  *Proof.* (a) $2(p-i)=(2p-1-i)-(i-1)$ gives the first identity. $q_{s_0}/w(s_0)=\binom p{s_0}$, and $q_{i+1}/q_i=\frac{p-i}{i+1}\cdot\frac{i+1}{2p-1-i}=\rho_i$ ([P1] `lem:prior`(b) and the proof of (c)); multiply for $i=s_0,\dots,k-1$.
   33  
   34  (b) First, $\rho_i\le\frac12e^{-(i-1)/(2p-2)}$ for $0\le i\le p-1$. For $i\ge1$ put $x=(i-1)/(2p-1-i)\in[0,1)$; since $2p-1-i\le 2p-2$, $x\ge(i-1)/(2p-2)$, and $\rho_i=\frac12(1-x)\le\frac12e^{-x}$. For $i=0$, $\rho_0=\frac12(1+\frac1{2p-1})\le\frac12e^{1/(2p-1)}\le\frac12e^{1/(2p-2)}$. Next, $\sum_{i=s_0}^{k-1}(i-1)=\sum_{t=s_0-1}^{k-2}t=\frac12[(k-1)(k-2)-(s_0-1)(s_0-2)]$ (valid also for $s_0=0$). Hence by (a), for $m+1\le k\le K$ (so $k>s_0$),
   35  $$\frac{q_k}{w(s_0)}\le\binom p{s_0}2^{-(k-s_0)}\exp\Big\{-\frac{(k-1)(k-2)-(s_0-1)(s_0-2)}{4(p-1)}\Big\}\le\binom p{s_0}2^{-(k-s_0)}e^{-\gamma_m},$$
   36  because $t\mapsto t(t-1)$ is nondecreasing on the integers $t\ge0$ and $k-1\ge m\ge0$. Summing, $\sum_{k\ge m+1}2^{-(k-s_0)}=2^{-(m-s_0)}$.
   37  
   38  (c) $R_m\ge q_{m+1}/w(s_0)$ because $m+1\le K$ and all terms are positive. For $1\le i\le m\ (\le p-1)$, $2\rho_i=\frac{2p-2i}{2p-1-i}$ and $\log(2\rho_i)=-\log\big(1+\frac{i-1}{2(p-i)}\big)\ge-\frac{i-1}{2(p-i)}\ge-\frac{i-1}{2(p-m)}$. Since $s_0\ge1$ every index in $\prod_{i=s_0}^m$ is $\ge1$; sum $\sum_{i=s_0}^m(i-1)=\frac12[m(m-1)-(s_0-1)(s_0-2)]$ and use (a) with $k=m+1$.
   39  
   40  (d) $\binom p{s_0}\le p^{s_0}/s_0!$, so $\binom p{s_0}2^{s_0-m}e^{-\gamma_m}\le(2p)^{s_0}2^{-m}e^{-\gamma_m}/s_0!$. For $m\ge s_0\ge1$, $m(m-1)\ge s_0(s_0-1)\ge(s_0-1)(s_0-2)$, so $\gamma_m\ge0$. $\square$
   41  
   42  **Reading.** By (a) the size marginal of BB(1,p) is geometric with ratio $\rho_i\approx\frac12$; the per-*model* ratio $w(k+1)/w(k)=(k+1)/(2p-1-k)\approx k/(2p)$ is cancelled by the multiplicity $\binom p{k+1}/\binom pk=(p-k)/(k+1)$. The exact tail therefore improves the locked one only by the factor $4\,s_0!\,e^{\gamma_m}$ ($\approx 36$ bits at $s_0=14$, plus $m^2/(4p)$ nats), not by a factor $p^{-(m-s_0)}$.
   43  
   44  ### Definition (new size cutoff)
   45  For $s_0\le K$ and real $\omega$:
   46  $$m^\sharp_n(\omega):=\min\{m\in\mathbb Z:\ m\ge s_0,\ R_m\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}\},\qquad m^\sharp_n:=m^\sharp_n(\tfrac12\log n).$$
   47  The minimum exists and $m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le K$, because $R_K=0$. It is computable exactly (`scripts/tail_bound.py`).
   48  
   49  ### Lemma E2 (location of $m^\sharp_n$; PROVED)
   50  Assume $s_0\le K$, $\omega\ge0$, and $s_0\ge1$ in (ii)–(iii) ($n\ge5$ if $s_0=0$ in (i)).
   51  
   52  **(i)** $s_0\le m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le\min\{K,\ m_n(\omega)\}$.
   53  
   54  **(ii)** $m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le\min\Big\{K,\ s_0+\Big\lceil\dfrac{\log\binom p{s_0}+\frac{s_0+1}2\log n+\omega}{\log2}\Big\rceil\Big\}$.
   55  
   56  **(iii)** If $m^\sharp:=m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le K-1$, then
   57  $$m^\sharp-s_0\ \ge\ \frac{\log\binom p{s_0}+\frac{s_0+1}2\log n+\omega}{\log2}-1-\frac{m^\sharp(m^\sharp-1)}{4(p-m^\sharp)\log2}.$$
   58  
   59  *Proof.* (i) $m^\sharp\ge s_0$ by definition and $m^\sharp\le K$ was noted. Let $m=m_n(\omega)$. Since $\omega\ge0$ and $\log(2p)\ge\log2$, $m\ge s_0$. By definition $2^{-m}\le(2p)^{-s_0}n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}$. If $s_0\ge1$: $\gamma_m\ge0$ (E1(d)), so E1(b) and $\binom p{s_0}2^{s_0}\le(2p)^{s_0}$ give $R_m\le(2p)^{s_0}2^{-m}\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}$, hence $m^\sharp\le m$. If $s_0=0$ and $n\ge5$: $m=\lceil(\frac12\log n+\omega)/\log2\rceil\ge2$, so $\gamma_m=[m(m-1)-2]/(4(p-1))\ge0$ and E1(b) gives $R_m\le2^{-m}\le n^{-1/2}e^{-\omega}$; again $m^\sharp\le m$.
   60  (ii) Let $m$ be the right-hand side (when it is $<K$). Then $2^{-(m-s_0)}\le\binom p{s_0}^{-1}n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}$ and E1(b) with $\gamma_m\ge0$ gives $R_m\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}$.
   61  (iii) At $m=m^\sharp\le K-1$ combine E1(c) with $R_m\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}$, take logarithms and drop $(s_0-1)(s_0-2)\ge0$. $\square$
   62  
   63  ### Proposition E3 (the exact-tail route cannot give $m_n=s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)$; PROVED)
   64  In R1 with $s_0\ge1$ fixed and $n^{a}\le p_n\le n^A$ for some fixed $0<a\le A$: either $m^\sharp_n=K$ or
   65  $$m^\sharp_n-s_0\ \ge\ \frac{s_0\log(p/s_0)+\frac{s_0+2}2\log n}{\log2}-1-o(1)\ \ge\ \frac{(s_0a+\frac{s_0+2}{2})\log n-s_0\log s_0}{\log 2}-1-o(1).$$
   66  Since $s_0\log n/\log p\le s_0/a=O(1)$, the brief's target scale $m_n=s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)$ is not reached by any bound of the form "Markov numerator over $S_0$-denominator" (the form of the locked T02(i) and of Theorem T02(i♯) below): such a bound is at least $R_m(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\cdot c$ with $R_m$ two-sided-controlled by E1.
   67  
   68  *Proof.* E2(iii) with $\omega=\frac12\log n$, $\binom p{s_0}\ge(p/s_0)^{s_0}$, and $m^\sharp\le m_n(\tfrac12\log n)=O(\log n)$ (E2(i), $p\le n^A$) so $m^{\sharp2}/(p-m^\sharp)\to0$ because $p\ge n^a$. $\square$
   69  
   70  *Remark (not a claim about the true posterior).* E3 is a barrier for the proof technique. Whether the *true* posterior needs $m_n-s_0\asymp s_0\log p$ under G and R is **OPEN**. Proposition D below shows that *some* growth, $m_n\ge(\tfrac12-o(1))\log_2 n$, is necessary in general.
   71  
   72  ---
   73  
   74  ## 2. Theorem T02(i♯): sharpened size tail with explicit constants (PROVED; candidate)
   75  
   76  Constants (as in [P1] §1 and `lem:den`): $b_-=b_0\sigma_*^2/2$, $b_+=b_0(2(\sigma_*^2+M)+1)$, $\kappa=(b_+/b_-)^{0.51}$, $\mathcal B_n=\{b_-\le b_0s_y^2\le b_+\}$, $c_{\rm IG}=\min_{v\in[\sigma_*^2,2\sigma_*^2]}\mathrm{IG}(v;0.51,b_+)$, $C_\Lambda=\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12+\mathbf 1\{s_0\ge1\}\frac{(1+\frac1{2\varphi_0^2})(M+\sigma_*^2)}{2\sigma_*^2}$, and
   77  $$c^\sharp:=\kappa^2/(c_{\rm IG}\sigma_*^2).$$
   78  
   79  **Theorem T02(i♯).** Assume G and R, and let $n$ be such that $s_0\le K$. For every integer $m$ define $\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}\ge0$ by
   80  $$\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)=R_m\,(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\;\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}\quad\text{if }R_m>0,\qquad\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}:=0\ \text{ if }R_m=0 .$$
   81  Then for every $L>c^{\sharp2}$,
   82  $$\sup_m P_0(\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}>L)\ \le\ \frac{8+24M/\sigma_*^2}{n-1}+\frac1{\sqrt L}+\frac{C_\Lambda}{\log(\sqrt L/c^\sharp)} .$$
   83  Consequently $\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_n\sup_mP_0(\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}>L)=0$, and for every deterministic real sequence $\omega_n$,
   84  $$\Pi(|S|>m^\sharp_n(\omega_n)\mid y)\le(1+\tfrac1n)^{s_0/2}e^{-\omega_n}\,\Theta^\sharp_{n,m^\sharp_n(\omega_n)}=O_{P_0}(e^{-\omega_n}).$$
   85  (When $R_m=0$, $\{S\in\Omega:|S|>m\}=\emptyset$ because $\varpi>0$ on $\Omega$, so $\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)=0$ and the definition is consistent.) The inequality is non-asymptotic: it holds at every $n$ with $s_0\le K$.
   86  
   87  **Changed step relative to [P1] `thm:T02i`:** the prior factor. [P1] bounded $\varpi(|S|>m)\le2^{1-m}$ (`lem:prior`(c)) and $\varpi(S_0)\ge\frac12(2p)^{-s_0}$ (`lem:prior`(d)) separately; here the ratio $R_m$ is kept exactly. For this we need the denominator bound of [P1] `lem:den` *before* the factor $\varpi(S_0)$ is bounded; we restate it.
   88  
   89  **Lemma den′** (= [P1] `lem:den` without its last factor). Under G, R and $s_0\le K$, with $\Lambda_n$ as in [P1] `lem:den`,
   90  $$\frac{m^c_{b_+}(S_0)}{f_0(y_c)}\ \ge\ (n+1)^{-s_0/2}\,c_{\rm IG}\,\sigma_*^2\,n^{-1/2}e^{-\Lambda_n},\qquad E_0\Lambda_n\le C_\Lambda .$$
   91  *Proof.* This is exactly what the paragraphs "Bound on $Q^c_{S_0}$", "Integral representation", "Lower bound on the exponent" and the first two sentences of "Assembling" in the proof of [P1] `lem:den` establish: restricting the $v$-integral to $[\sigma_*^2,\sigma_*^2(1+n^{-1/2})]$ (length $\sigma_*^2n^{-1/2}$, IG density $\ge c_{\rm IG}$, exponent $\ge-\Lambda_n$) gives $m^c_{b_+}(S_0)/f_0(y_c)\ge D_{S_0}^{-1/2}c_{\rm IG}\sigma_*^2n^{-1/2}e^{-\Lambda_n}$, and $D_{S_0}\le(n+1)^{s_0}$ ([P1] `lem:spec`(e)). The bound on $E_0\Lambda_n$ is the last paragraph of that proof. The factor $\varpi(S_0)\ge\frac12(2p)^{-s_0}$ is not used. $\square$
   92  
   93  *Proof of T02(i♯).* Fix $n$ with $s_0\le K$ and an integer $m$ with $R_m>0$ (otherwise there is nothing to prove). Put $E_m=\{|S|>m\}$, $v_m:=\varpi(E_m)=R_m\varpi(S_0)>0$, $N_m:=I_{b_-}(E_m)/f_0(y_c)$ and $\Theta^{(1)}_{n,m}:=N_m/v_m\ge0$. Since $b_-$ is data-free, [P1] `lem:num` gives $E_0N_m=v_m$, i.e. $E_0\Theta^{(1)}_{n,m}=1$. On $\mathcal B_n$, [P1] `thm:Ta` and Lemma den′ give
   94  $$\Pi(E_m\mid y)\le\kappa^2\frac{I_{b_-}(E_m)}{\varpi(S_0)m^c_{b_+}(S_0)}=\kappa^2\frac{v_m\Theta^{(1)}_{n,m}}{\varpi(S_0)\,m^c_{b_+}(S_0)/f_0(y_c)}\le R_m(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\cdot c^\sharp e^{\Lambda_n}\Theta^{(1)}_{n,m}.$$
   95  So on $\mathcal B_n$, $\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}\le c^\sharp e^{\Lambda_n}\Theta^{(1)}_{n,m}$. For $L>c^{\sharp2}$, $\{c^\sharp e^{\Lambda_n}\Theta^{(1)}>L\}\subseteq\{\Theta^{(1)}>\sqrt L\}\cup\{c^\sharp e^{\Lambda_n}>\sqrt L\}$, so
   96  $$P_0(\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}>L)\le P_0(\mathcal B_n^c)+P_0(\Theta^{(1)}_{n,m}>\sqrt L)+P_0\big(\Lambda_n>\log(\sqrt L/c^\sharp)\big)\le P_0(\mathcal B_n^c)+\frac1{\sqrt L}+\frac{C_\Lambda}{\log(\sqrt L/c^\sharp)},$$
   97  by Markov's inequality ($\Theta^{(1)}\ge0$, $\Lambda_n\ge0$). $P_0(\mathcal B_n^c)\le(8+24M/\sigma_*^2)/(n-1)$ by [P1] `thm:T01iii`. The right side does not depend on $m$. For the consequence take $m=m^\sharp_n(\omega_n)$: $R_m\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega_n}$, hence $\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega_n}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\,\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}=(1+\frac1n)^{s_0/2}e^{-\omega_n}\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}$, and $P_0(\Theta^\sharp_{n,m}>L)\le\sup_{m'}P_0(\Theta^\sharp_{n,m'}>L)$. $\square$
   98  
   99  *Remark.* As in [P1], only $\|\mu\|^2\le nM$, $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0})\ge\varphi_0^2$ and $s_0\le K$ are used from R; no eigenvalue condition on other models; $p\le n^A$ is not used.
  100  
  101  ---
  102  
  103  ## 3. Proposition D: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the target scale without SE (COUNTEREXAMPLE, reproducible)
  104  
  105  **Design.** $n\ge3$, $2\le p$ (e.g. $p=n$, so $A=1$), $x\in\mathbb R^n$ fixed with $\|Cx\|^2=n-1$, $X^r=[x,\dots,x]$ ($p$ identical columns), $\beta^*=(\beta_1,0,\dots,0)$ with fixed $\beta_1\ne0$, any $\alpha^*$, $\sigma_*>0$. Then $s_0=1$, $S_0=\{1\}$, $\tilde x:=Cx$ is every standardised column, $\|\mu\|^2/n=\beta_1^2(n-1)/n\le\beta_1^2=:M$, $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0})=1$: **G and R hold** (SE fails at size 2).
  106  
  107  **Claim.** With $E_n:=\{m(\emptyset)\le m(\{1\})\}$, $P_0(E_n)\to1$, and on $E_n$, for every integer $0\le m\le K-1$,
  108  $$\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\ \ge\ 2^{-(m+4)}\exp\Big\{-\frac{m(m-1)}{4(p-m)}\Big\}.$$
  109  Consequently, for any deterministic $m_n\le\sqrt p$ with $\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)=O_{P_0}(n^{-1/2})$, necessarily $m_n\ge\frac12\log_2n-O(1)$; in particular no cutoff $m_n=s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)=1+O(1)$ (here $p=n$) works, and more generally $\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)=O_{P_0}(e^{-\omega_n})$ forces $m_n\ge\omega_n/\log2-O(1)$.
  110  
  111  *Proof.* Let $S$ have $|S|=k\ge1$. Then $X_S=\tilde x\mathbf 1_k^\top$, $G_S=N\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^\top$ (eigenvalues $kN,0,\dots,0$), so $D_S=\frac{(n+1)kN+1}{kN+1}=:D_k$; $H_S=(n+1)N\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^\top+I$ has $\mathbf 1$ as eigenvector with eigenvalue $(n+1)Nk+1$, so with $c:=\tilde x^\top y$, $z_S=c\mathbf 1$ and $Q_S=N-\frac{nkc^2}{(n+1)Nk+1}=:Q_k$ (using $y^\top y=N$). Hence $m(S)=:m_k$ depends on $|S|$ only, and $\Pi(|S|=k\mid y)=q_km_k/\sum_{k'=0}^Kq_{k'}m_{k'}$ ($W_K$ cancels).
  112  
  113  *Two-sided comparison of $m_k$, $k\ge1$, with $m_1$ (deterministic).* $D_k\le n+1$ and $D_1\ge\frac{(n+1)N}{N+1}$, so $(D_1/D_k)^{1/2}\ge(N/(N+1))^{1/2}\ge(2/3)^{1/2}$; and $k\mapsto\frac k{(n+1)Nk+1}$ is increasing, so $Q_k\le Q_1$ and $(2b_0+Q_k)^{-\nu}\ge(2b_0+Q_1)^{-\nu}$. Thus $m_k\ge(2/3)^{1/2}m_1$. Conversely $D_k\ge D_1$, and $0\le Q_1-Q_k\le nc^2\big[\frac1{(n+1)N}-\frac1{(n+1)N+1}\big]\le\frac{n}{(n+1)^2}\le\frac1n$ using $c^2\le\|\tilde x\|^2\|y\|^2=N^2$; with $Q_k\ge\|y\|^2/(n+1)=N/(n+1)$ ([P1] `lem:spec`(b)), $\frac{2b_0+Q_1}{2b_0+Q_k}\le1+\frac{n+1}{nN}\le1+\frac2n$ ($n\ge3$), so $m_k/m_1\le(1+\frac2n)^{\nu}\le e^{2\nu/n}=e^{1+0.02/n}\le e^{1.01}$.
  114  
  115  *Tail.* On $E_n$, using $q_0=\frac12$ and $\sum_kq_k\le1$ ([P1] `lem:prior`(a)):
  116  $$\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\ge\frac{(2/3)^{1/2}m_1\sum_{k>m}q_k}{q_0m_0+e^{1.01}m_1\sum_{k\ge1}q_k}\ge\frac{(2/3)^{1/2}}{\frac12+e^{1.01}}\,q_{m+1}\ge\tfrac14\,q_{m+1}.$$
  117  By E1(a) with $s_0=0$: $q_{m+1}=\frac12\rho_0\prod_{i=1}^m\rho_i$ with $\rho_0\ge\frac12$ and, as in E1(c), $\prod_{i=1}^m\rho_i\ge2^{-m}e^{-m(m-1)/(4(p-m))}$ ($m\le K-1\le p-1$). So $q_{m+1}\ge2^{-(m+2)}e^{-m(m-1)/(4(p-m))}$.
  118  
  119  *$P_0(E_n)\to1$.* $m_0/m_1=D_1^{1/2}\big(\frac{2b_0+Q_1}{2b_0+N}\big)^\nu$ and $N-Q_1=\frac{nc^2}{(n+1)N+1}$. With $u:=c^2/N^2\in[0,1]$ (squared sample correlation of $x$ and $y^r$), $\frac{2b_0+Q_1}{2b_0+N}=1-u\frac{nN^2}{((n+1)N+1)(N+2b_0)}\le1-\frac u2$ (the fraction is $\ge\frac12$ for $n\ge3$: $((n+1)N+1)(N+0.02)\le1.01(n+1.5)N^2\le2nN^2$). So $m_0/m_1\le(n+1)^{1/2}e^{-\nu u/2}\le(n+1)^{1/2}e^{-nu/4}$, and $E_n\supseteq\{u\ge2\log(n+1)/n\}$. Now $Cy^r=\beta_1\tilde x+C\varepsilon$, so $u=\frac{(\beta_1N+\tilde x^\top\varepsilon)^2}{N(\beta_1^2N+2\beta_1\tilde x^\top\varepsilon+\|C\varepsilon\|^2)}$ with $\tilde x^\top\varepsilon\sim N(0,\sigma_*^2N)$ and $\|C\varepsilon\|^2/\sigma_*^2\sim\chi^2_N$. By Chebyshev, $\tilde x^\top\varepsilon/N\to0$ and $\|C\varepsilon\|^2/N\to\sigma_*^2$ in probability, so $u\to\beta_1^2/(\beta_1^2+\sigma_*^2)>0$ in probability while $2\log(n+1)/n\to0$.
  120  
  121  *Consequence.* If $\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)=O_{P_0}(e^{-\omega_n})$ with $m_n\le\min(\sqrt p,K-1)$, then for some $L$ and all large $n$, $P_0(\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)\le Le^{-\omega_n})\ge\frac12$, which meets $E_n$ for large $n$, giving $2^{-(m_n+4)}e^{-1/2}\le Le^{-\omega_n}$ (as $m_n(m_n-1)/(4(p-m_n))\le\frac12$ once $\sqrt p\le p/2$), i.e. $m_n\ge\omega_n/\log 2-\log_2L-5$. (If $m_n\ge K$ the tail is $0$; that is consistent: $K=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\gg\frac12\log_2 n$.) $\square$
  122

  127  ## 4. Restricted eigenvalue hypotheses and bookkeeping
  128  
  129  **Hypotheses (new).** Let $j_0:=\lceil(2A+1)s_0\rceil+1$ (this is $j_*$ of [P3]; it depends only on $s_0,A$) and $g_0>0$ a fixed constant.
  130  
  131  - **SE$_\lambda(j_0)$** [anchored, normalised, bounded size]: $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0\cup J})\ge\varphi_0^2$ for every $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $|J|\le j_0$ and $S_0\cup J\ne\emptyset$.
  132  - **SE$_w(m;g_0)$** [anchored, unnormalised]: $\lambda_{\min}(G_{S_0\cup J})\ge g_0$ (equivalently $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0\cup J})\ge g_0/(n-1)$) for every $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $|J|\le m$ and $S_0\cup J\ne\emptyset$.
  133  
  134  These are restrictions of SE to the **comparison unions** $S\cup S_0$ used by the proofs. The locked SE (all $T$ with $|T|\le\min(p,m_n+s_0)$, constant $\varphi_0^2$) implies SE$_\lambda(j_0)$ (as $j_0\le m_n$ for large $n$) and SE$_w(m^\sharp_n;\varphi_0^2)$ (as $m^\sharp_n\le m_n$ by E2(i), and $(n-1)\varphi_0^2\ge\varphi_0^2$). So the new hypotheses are weaker.

  136  **Lemma I (interlacing; standard).** If $\emptyset\ne T\subseteq T'$, then $\lambda_{\min}(G_T)\ge\lambda_{\min}(G_{T'})$. *Proof.* For $v\in\mathbb R^T$, $v^\top G_Tv=\tilde v^\top G_{T'}\tilde v$ with $\tilde v$ the zero-padding, and $\|\tilde v\|=\|v\|$. $\square$
  137  
  138  **Lemma B (what the proofs need; PROVED).** Assume R, SE$_\lambda(j_0)$ and SE$_w(m^\sharp_n;g_0)$.
  139  - **(B1)** For $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $1\le|J|\le m^\sharp_n$: $\lambda_{\min}(G_{S_0\cup J})\ge g_0>0$, so $X_{c,S_0\cup J}$ has full column rank, $P_{S_0\cup J}-P_{S_0}$ is an orthogonal projection of rank $|J|$, and under G, $\chi^2_J:=\sigma_*^{-2}\|(P_{S_0\cup J}-P_{S_0})e\|^2\sim\chi^2_{|J|}$ exactly; and $D_{S_0\cup J}/D_{S_0}\ge[(n+1)(1+1/g_0)^{-1}]^{|J|}$.
  140  - **(B2)** For underfitting $S$ (i.e. $S_0\not\subseteq S$) with $|J'(S)|\le j_0$, $S'=S\cup S_0$: $\lambda_{\min}(G_{S'})\ge N\varphi_0^2$; if $S\ne\emptyset$, $\lambda_{\min}(G_S)\ge N\varphi_0^2$; $P_{S'}-P_S$ is an orthogonal projection of rank $|J(S)|$; under G, $N_S/\sigma_*^2\sim\chi^2_{|J(S)|}$.
  141  - **(B3)** For $S\subseteq T$, $T\ne\emptyset$, with $S=\emptyset$ or $\lambda_{\min}(G_S)\ge N\varphi_0^2$, and every $u\in\mathbb R^N$: $u^\top(M_T-M_S)u\le\frac n{n+1}\big[\|(P_T-P_S)u\|^2+\eta_n\|P_Su\|^2\big]$. (Upper half of [P3] `cor:diff`, with the eigenvalue condition on $S$ only.)

  143  *Proof.* (B1) SE$_w$; full column rank because $G_{S_0\cup J}\succ0$; then $\mathrm{col}(X_{c,S_0})\subseteq\mathrm{col}(X_{c,S_0\cup J})$ have dimensions $s_0$ and $s_0+|J|$, so the difference of the projections is the projection onto the orthogonal complement, of rank $|J|$; $e\sim N_N(0,\sigma_*^2I)$ ([P3] `lem:red`(b)).   168  - **The frozen-plan sentence "cuts m_n from about 200 to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p), so SE on sets of size ≤ m_n + s₀ ≤ K becomes meaningful at n = 200" is wrong on both counts.**

  173  - **A route that might give m − s₀ = O(log n) is a CONJECTURE, not attempted in full.** It would need SE_w at *all* sizes ≤ K, a per-eigendirection truncation of the Markov moment, and handling of non-supersets through a weak residual condition.

  176  ## 5. n = 200 disclosure paragraph (for the paper)
  177  
  178  > *Scope at the study's sample size.* Theorem 1 (T03♯) and its lemmas are asymptotic statements for a triangular array with s₀ fixed and p_n ≤ n^A; they are not numerical guarantees at n = 200, p ∈ {500, 1000}, s₀ = 14 (and the generator's rule s₀ = ⌊√n⌋ is outside their scope). In the original formulation the sparse-eigenvalue premise ranged over all subsets of up to 215 (p = 500) or 229 (p = 1000) columns, which is impossible at rank ≤ 199. In the restated version the premise is anchored at the true support and restricted to the comparison sets S₀ ∪ J that the proof uses: a normalised bound λ_min(R_{S₀∪J}) ≥ φ₀² for |J| ≤ j₀ (62 and 66 columns) and an unnormalised non-degeneracy bound λ_min(X_{S₀∪J}ᵀX_{S₀∪J}) ≥ g₀ for |J| ≤ min(m♯_n, K) = 100 (114 columns, because the model-size cap K = ⌊n/2⌋ = 100 binds at n = 200; the exact Beta-Binomial tail alone would give 146 and 168 extra variables). These conditions are no longer excluded by rank, but they are not verified for the realised designs, and in correlated designs the normalised constant can be as small as φ₀² ≈ 0.01–0.03. The beta-min condition remains far from the executed signals: the proof's sufficient constant requires θ*² ≥ 27.5/φ₀² (p = 500) and 30.6/φ₀² (p = 1000) on the standardised scale, against executed values 0.64 (c = 1) and 0.16 (c = 0.5), a shortfall of at least 43× (p = 500) and 48× (p = 1000) even with φ₀² = 1. This is a limitation of the proof constant, not evidence that the signals are weak: a heuristic orthogonal-design scale is ≈ 0.09. The rate √(log n/n) = 0.163 carries unspecified constants, and the proof's own deterministic thresholds hold only from n ≈ 10⁵. The empirical recovery rates at n = 200 are therefore evidence in their own right, not an instance of the theorem.

   40  \section{Setting and conventions}\label{sec:setting}

   42  \paragraph{Data.} $n\ge3$, $p\ge1$, $C=I_n-\mathbf 1\mathbf 1\tr/n$, $X=CX^rD_x^{-1}$, $\sy^2=\|Cy^r\|^2/(n-1)>0$, $y=Cy^r/\sy$. $U\in\R^{n\times(n-1)}$ is a fixed (non-random) matrix with $U\tr U=I_{n-1}$ and $UU\tr=C$.    43  \begin{equation}\label{eq:UX}
   44  \begin{gathered}
   45  X=UU\tr X=U\Xc,\qquad y=UU\tr y^r/\sy=U\yc/\sy,\\
   46  \Xc\tr\Xc=X\tr X,\qquad \|\yc\|^2=(y^r)\tr Cy^r=(n-1)\sy^2 .
   47  \end{gathered}
   48  \end{equation}

   60  \section{Deterministic preliminaries}\label{sec:prelim}
   61  
   62  Throughout this section $n\ge 3$ is a fixed number, $a\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ are integers, $\mathsf{A}\in\R^{a\times k}$, $Y\in\R^a$, and
   63  \[
   64  G=\mathsf{A}\tr \mathsf{A},\quad H=(n+1)G+I_k,\quad D=\frac{\det H}{\det(G+I_k)},\]\[ Q=Y\tr Y-n(\mathsf{A}\tr Y)\tr H^{-1}\mathsf{A}\tr Y,\quad \mathsf{M}=n\mathsf{A}H^{-1}\mathsf{A}\tr .
   65  \]
   66  $P_{\mathsf{A}}$ denotes the orthogonal projection onto the column span of $\mathsf{A}$ ($P_{\mathsf{A}}=0$ if $k=0$).
   67  
   68  \begin{lemma}[Gaussian slab integral]\label{lem:slab}
   69  For every $v>0$,
   70  \[
   71  \int_{\R^k}\N_a(Y;\mathsf{A}\theta,vI_a)\,\N_k\big(\theta;0,nv(G+I)^{-1}\big)\,d\theta=(2\pi v)^{-a/2}D^{-1/2}e^{-Q/(2v)},
   72  \]
   73  and the integrand, normalised in $\theta$, is the density of $\N_k(nH^{-1}\mathsf{A}\tr Y,\;nvH^{-1})$. Moreover $Q=\min_\theta\{\|Y-\mathsf{A}\theta\|^2+\theta\tr(G+I)\theta/n\}\ge0$. (For $k=0$ the integral is the value of the first factor, $D=1$, $Q=Y\tr Y$.)
   74  \end{lemma}
   75  \begin{proof}
   76  For $k=0$ there is nothing to prove. Let $k\ge1$; $G+I$ and $H$ are positive definite. The exponent of the integrand is $-\frac1{2v}J(\theta)$ with
   77  \[
   78  J(\theta)=\|Y-\mathsf{A}\theta\|^2+\tfrac1n\theta\tr(G+I)\theta=Y\tr Y-2\theta\tr \mathsf{A}\tr Y+\tfrac1n\theta\tr H\theta ,
   79  \]
   80  since $G+\frac1n(G+I)=\frac1nH$. With $m=nH^{-1}\mathsf{A}\tr Y$, completing the square gives $J(\theta)=(\theta-m)\tr\frac Hn(\theta-m)+Y\tr Y-m\tr\frac Hn m$, and $m\tr\frac Hnm=n(\mathsf{A}\tr Y)\tr H^{-1}\mathsf{A}\tr Y$, so $J(\theta)=(\theta-m)\tr\frac Hn(\theta-m)+Q$. This proves the minimum representation of $Q$ and $Q\ge0$, and shows that the normalised integrand is $\N_k(m,nvH^{-1})$. The constant in front of $e^{-J/(2v)}$ is $(2\pi v)^{-a/2}(2\pi)^{-k/2}\det(nv(G+I)^{-1})^{-1/2}$, and $\int e^{-(\theta-m)\tr H(\theta-m)/(2nv)}d\theta=(2\pi)^{k/2}\det(nvH^{-1})^{1/2}$. The product of the determinant factors is $\big((nv)^{-k}\det(G+I)\big)^{1/2}\big((nv)^k/\det H\big)^{1/2}=D^{-1/2}$.
   81  \end{proof}
   82  
   83  \begin{lemma}[inverse-gamma integral]\label{lem:IGint}
   84  For $\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b>0$: $\int_0^\infty v^{-\mathfrak a-1}e^{-\mathfrak b/v}dv=\Gamma(\mathfrak a)\mathfrak b^{-\mathfrak a}$.
   85  \end{lemma}
   86  \begin{proof}
   87  Substitute $t=\mathfrak b/v$: the integral becomes $\mathfrak b^{-\mathfrak a}\int_0^\infty t^{\mathfrak a-1}e^{-t}dt$.
   88  \end{proof}
   89  
   90  \begin{lemma}[smoother and determinant]\label{lem:spec}
   91  Let $h(\lambda)=\frac{n\lambda}{(n+1)\lambda+1}$ and $f(\lambda)=\frac{(n+1)\lambda+1}{\lambda+1}$ for $\lambda\ge0$.
   92  \begin{enumerate}
   93  \item[(a)] $\mathsf{M}=h(\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr)$ (functional calculus), and $Q=Y\tr(I-\mathsf{M})Y$.
   94  \item[(b)] $0\preceq \mathsf{M}\preceq\frac n{n+1}P_{\mathsf{A}}$; hence $I-\mathsf{M}\succeq I-P_{\mathsf{A}}$ and $I-\mathsf{M}\succeq\frac1{n+1}I$, so $Q\ge\|(I-P_{\mathsf{A}})Y\|^2$ and $Q\ge\|Y\|^2/(n+1)$.
   95  \item[(c)] If $k\ge1$ and $\lambda_{\min}(G)\ge g>0$, then $\mathsf{M}\succeq\frac n{n+1}\big(1-\frac1{(n+1)g}\big)P_{\mathsf{A}}$ and $I-\mathsf{M}\preceq(I-P_{\mathsf{A}})+\gamma P_{\mathsf{A}}$ with $\gamma=\frac1{n+1}\big(1+\frac1g\big)$.
   96  \item[(d)] If $\mathsf{A}'$ is obtained from $\mathsf{A}$ by adjoining columns, then $\mathsf{M}_{\mathsf{A}}\preceq \mathsf{M}_{\mathsf{A}'}$; hence $Q_{\mathsf{A}}\ge Q_{\mathsf{A}'}$.
   97  \item[(e)] $D=\prod_{i=1}^kf(\lambda_i(G))$; in particular $1\le D\le(n+1)^k$. If $\mathsf{A}'$ is $\mathsf{A}$ with $j\ge1$ adjoined columns, $G'=\mathsf{A}'^{\top}\mathsf{A}'$ and $\lambda_{\min}(G')\ge g>0$, then $D'/D\ge f(g)^j\ge\big[(n+1)(1+1/g)^{-1}\big]^j$.
   98  \end{enumerate}
   99  \end{lemma}
  100  \begin{proof}
  101  (a) For $c=n+1$, $\mathsf{A}(c\mathsf{A}\tr \mathsf{A}+I)=(c\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr+I)\mathsf{A}$, so $\mathsf{A}(c\mathsf{A}\tr \mathsf{A}+I)^{-1}=(c\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr+I)^{-1}\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{M}=n(c\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr+I)^{-1}\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr=h(\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr)$, the two factors commuting. Then $Q=Y\tr Y-Y\tr \mathsf{M}Y$ by definition of $\mathsf{M}$.
  102  
  103  (b) $h$ is increasing, $h(0)=0$ and $h<\frac n{n+1}$. The eigenvectors of $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr$ with nonzero eigenvalue span the column space of $\mathsf{A}$, and $\mathsf{M}$ vanishes on its orthogonal complement; so the eigenvalues of $\mathsf{M}$ lie in $[0,\frac n{n+1})$ on the column space and are $0$ off it. Thus $\mathsf{M}\preceq\frac n{n+1}P_{\mathsf{A}}\preceq P_{\mathsf{A}}$, and $I-\mathsf{M}\succeq I-\frac n{n+1}P_{\mathsf{A}}\succeq\frac1{n+1}I$.
  104  
  105  (c) The nonzero eigenvalues of $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr$ are those of $G$, all $\ge g$, and their eigenvectors span the column space. Since $h(\lambda)=\frac n{n+1}\big(1-\frac1{(n+1)\lambda+1}\big)\ge\frac n{n+1}\big(1-\frac1{(n+1)g}\big)$ for $\lambda\ge g$, the first claim follows. For the second: on the column space, $1-h(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda+1}{(n+1)\lambda+1}\le\frac{\lambda+1}{(n+1)\lambda}=\frac1{n+1}\big(1+\frac1\lambda\big)\le\gamma$; off it, $I-\mathsf{M}$ acts as the identity, which is $I-P_{\mathsf{A}}$ there.
  106  
  107  (d) $h(\lambda)=\frac n{n+1}\big(1-((n+1)\lambda+1)^{-1}\big)$. If $0\preceq B_1\preceq B_2$ then $((n+1)B_2+I)^{-1}\preceq((n+1)B_1+I)^{-1}$, so $h(B_1)\preceq h(B_2)$. Apply this with $B_1=\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}\tr\preceq \mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}'^{\top}=B_2$; then use (a).
  108  
  109  (e) $H$ and $G+I$ are polynomials in $G$, so $D=\prod_if(\lambda_i(G))$; $f$ is increasing with $f(0)=1$ and $f<n+1$. Order eigenvalues increasingly. $G$ is a principal submatrix of $G'$ (columns of $\mathsf{A}$ first), so Cauchy interlacing gives $\lambda_i(G)\le\lambda_{i+j}(G')$ for $1\le i\le k$, whence $D\le\prod_{i=1}^kf(\lambda_{i+j}(G'))$ and
  110  $D'/D\ge\prod_{i=1}^{j}f(\lambda_i(G'))\ge f(g)^j$. Finally $f(g)\ge\frac{(n+1)g}{g+1}=(n+1)(1+1/g)^{-1}$.
  111  \end{proof}
  112  
  113  \begin{lemma}[the capped $\mathrm{BB}(1,p)$ prior]\label{lem:prior}
  114  \begin{enumerate}
  115  \item[(a)] $w(k)=B(1+k,2p-k)/B(1,p)$ for $0\le k\le p$, and $\sum_{k=0}^p\binom pkw(k)=1$; hence $\frac12=w(0)\le W_K\le1$.
  116  \item[(b)] $w(k+1)/w(k)=(k+1)/(2p-k-1)$ for $0\le k\le p-1$.
  117  \item[(c)] For every integer $m$: $\vp(\{S\in\Om:|S|>m\})\le 2^{1-m}$.
  118  \item[(d)] If $s_0\le K$, then $\vp(S_0)\ge\frac12(2p)^{-s_0}$.
  119  \item[(e)] For $j\ge1$ with $s_0+j\le p$: $\binom{p-s_0}{j}\frac{w(s_0+j)}{w(s_0)}\le2\binom{s_0+j}{j}2^{-j}\le2(j+1)^{s_0}2^{-j}$.
  120  \end{enumerate}
  121  \end{lemma}
  122  \begin{proof}
  123  (a) $B(1+k,2p-k)=k!(2p-k-1)!/(2p)!$ and $B(1,p)=1/p$, so the ratio is $\frac{k!(2p-1-k)!}{2(2p-1)!}=\frac12\binom{2p-1}{k}^{-1}=w(k)$. By the binomial theorem,
  124  $\sum_k\binom pk\int_0^1t^k(1-t)^{p-k}\frac{(1-t)^{p-1}}{B(1,p)}dt=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^{p-1}}{B(1,p)}dt=1$, and the $k$-th integral is $B(1+k,2p-k)/B(1,p)$. The bounds on $W_K$ follow since all terms are positive and the $k=0$ term is $w(0)=\frac12$.
  125  
  126  (b) $w(k+1)/w(k)=\binom{2p-1}{k}\big/\binom{2p-1}{k+1}=(k+1)/(2p-1-k)$.
  127  
  128  (c) Put $q_k=\binom pkw(k)$. By (b), $q_{k+1}/q_k=\frac{p-k}{k+1}\cdot\frac{k+1}{2p-k-1}=\frac{p-k}{2p-k-1}$, which is $\le\frac12$ iff $k\ge1$. Also $q_1=\frac{p}{2(2p-1)}\le\frac12$. Hence $q_k\le2^{-(k-1)}q_1\le2^{-k}$ for $1\le k\le p$, and for $m\ge0$, $\sum_{k>m}q_k\le\sum_{k\ge m+1}2^{-k}=2^{-m}$. Then $\vp(|S|>m)=\sum_{m<k\le K}q_k/W_K\le2\cdot2^{-m}$ by (a). For $m<0$ the bound exceeds $1$.
  129  
  130  (d) $\vp(S_0)=w(s_0)/W_K\ge w(s_0)=\frac12\binom{2p-1}{s_0}^{-1}\ge\frac12(2p-1)^{-s_0}\ge\frac12(2p)^{-s_0}$.
  131  
  132  (e) Write both factors as products over $i=0,\dots,j-1$, using (b):
  133  \[
  134  \binom{p-s_0}{j}\frac{w(s_0+j)}{w(s_0)}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}\frac{p-s_0-i}{i+1}\cdot\frac{s_0+i+1}{2p-s_0-i-1}=\binom{s_0+j}{j}\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}\frac{p-s_0-i}{2p-s_0-i-1}.
  135  \]
  136  The denominators are $\ge 2p-s_0-j\ge p\ge1$. A factor is $\le\frac12$ iff $s_0+i\ge1$; this fails only for $s_0=0,i=0$, where the factor is $p/(2p-1)\le1$. So the product is $\le2\cdot2^{-j}$. Finally $\binom{s_0+j}{j}=\prod_{i=1}^{s_0}\frac{j+i}{i}\le(j+1)^{s_0}$.
  137  \end{proof}
  138  
  139  \begin{lemma}[chi-square facts]\label{lem:chi}
  140  Let $\chi^2_r$ denote a chi-square variable with $r\ge0$ degrees of freedom ($\chi^2_0\equiv0$).
  141  \begin{enumerate}
  142  \item[(a)] If $r\le d$ and $x\ge0$, then $\Prob(\chi^2_r\ge 2d\log2+4x)\le e^{-x}$.
  143  \item[(b)] For $d\ge1$ and $t>0$: $\Prob(|\chi^2_d-d|>t)\le 2d/t^2$, and $\E|\chi^2_d-d|\le\sqrt{2d}$.
  144  \item[(c)] For $d\ge1$ and $\tau>0$: $\E\big[e^{\chi^2_d/2}\mathbf 1\{\chi^2_d\le\tau\}\big]=\frac{(\tau/2)^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)}\le\big(\frac{e\tau}{d}\big)^{d/2}$.
  145  \end{enumerate}
  146  \end{lemma}
  147  \begin{proof}
  148  (a) $\E e^{\chi^2_r/4}=(1-\frac12)^{-r/2}=2^{r/2}\le2^{d/2}$, so by Markov's inequality the probability is at most $2^{d/2}e^{-(2d\log2+4x)/4}=e^{-x}$.
  149  (b) $\mathrm{Var}(\chi^2_d)=2d$; Chebyshev and Cauchy--Schwarz.
  150  (c) The density of $\chi^2_d$ is $x^{d/2-1}e^{-x/2}/(2^{d/2}\Gamma(d/2))$, so the expectation is $\int_0^\tau x^{d/2-1}dx/(2^{d/2}\Gamma(d/2))=\tau^{d/2}/(2^{d/2}\frac d2\Gamma(\frac d2))$. The bound uses $\Gamma(x+1)\ge\int_x^\infty t^xe^{-t}dt\ge x^xe^{-x}$.
  151  \end{proof}

  153  \section{T01(i): the contrast identity}\label{sec:T01i}
  154  
  155  \begin{proposition}[closed forms]\label{prop:closed}
  156  For every valid input, $S\in\Om$ and $b>0$:
  157  \begin{align}
  158  m(S)&:=\iint\N_n(y;X_S\beta,\sigma^2I_n)\,\N_k\big(\beta;0,n\sigma^2(G_S+I)^{-1}\big)\IG(\sigma^2;a_0,b_0)\,d\beta\,d\sigma^2\nonumber\\
  159  &=\frac{(2b_0)^{a_0}\Gamma(\nu)}{\pi^{n/2}\Gamma(a_0)}D_S^{-1/2}(2b_0+Q_S)^{-\nu},\label{eq:m}\\
  160  m^c_b(S)&=(2\pi)^{-(n-1)/2}\frac{b^{0.51}\Gamma(\nu)}{\Gamma(0.51)}D_S^{-1/2}\big(b+Q^c_S/2\big)^{-\nu}.\label{eq:mc}
  161  \end{align}
  162  So the integral in \eqref{eq:m} is the method's $m(S)$. Under the contrast model at rate $b$ given $S$ and $\yc$, $v\sim\IG(\nu,b+Q^c_S/2)$ and $\theta_S\mid v\sim\N_k(nH_S^{-1}z^c_S,nvH_S^{-1})$.
  163  \end{proposition}
  164  \begin{proof}
  165  By Tonelli, integrate $\beta$ first using Lemma~\ref{lem:slab} with $a=n$, $\mathsf{A}=X_S$, $Y=y$. This gives $(2\pi\sigma^2)^{-n/2}D_S^{-1/2}e^{-Q_S/(2\sigma^2)}$. Then by Lemma~\ref{lem:IGint} with $\mathfrak a=a_0+n/2=\nu$ and $\mathfrak b=b_0+Q_S/2>0$,
  166  \[
  167  m(S)=(2\pi)^{-n/2}D_S^{-1/2}\frac{b_0^{a_0}}{\Gamma(a_0)}\Gamma(\nu)(b_0+Q_S/2)^{-\nu}
  168  =\frac{(2b_0)^{a_0}\Gamma(\nu)}{\pi^{n/2}\Gamma(a_0)}D_S^{-1/2}(2b_0+Q_S)^{-\nu},
  169  \]
  170  using $(b_0+Q/2)^{-\nu}=2^\nu(2b_0+Q)^{-\nu}$ and $2^{-n/2+\nu}=2^{a_0}$. For \eqref{eq:mc}, use Lemma~\ref{lem:slab} with $a=n-1$, $\mathsf{A}=X_{c,S}$ (so $\mathsf{A}\tr\mathsf{A}=G_S$), $Y=\yc$; then Lemma~\ref{lem:IGint} with $\mathfrak a=0.51+(n-1)/2=\nu$ and $\mathfrak b=b+Q^c_S/2$. The conditional law of $\theta_S$ is the normalised integrand of Lemma~\ref{lem:slab}. The $v$-marginal is proportional to $v^{-(n-1)/2}e^{-Q^c_S/(2v)}v^{-1.51}e^{-b/v}=v^{-\nu-1}e^{-(b+Q^c_S/2)/v}$.
  171  \end{proof}
  172  
  173  \begin{theorem}[T01(i)]\label{thm:T01i}
  174  For every valid input, the joint transformed posterior of $(S,\theta_S,v)$ equals $\Pi_{b}$ with $b=b_0\sy^2$. For every $S\in\Om$, $m(S)=c_n(\sy)\,m^c_{b_0\sy^2}(S)$ with $c_n(s)=s^{n-1}\Gamma(0.51)/(\sqrt{2\pi b_0}\,\Gamma(0.01))$. Moreover $z^c_S=\sy z_S$, $Q^c_S=\sy^2Q_S$, $Z=c_n(\sy)Z^c_{b_0\sy^2}$,
  175  \[
  176  \mathrm{BF}(S)=\frac{m^c_{b_0\sy^2}(S)}{m^c_{b_0\sy^2}(\emptyset)},\qquad \pi(S)=\frac{\vp(S)m^c_{b_0\sy^2}(S)}{Z^c_{b_0\sy^2}},
  177  \]
  178  and the conditionals are $v\mid S,y\sim\IG(\nu,b_0\sy^2+Q^c_S/2)$ and $\theta_S\mid v,S,y\sim\N_k(nH_S^{-1}z^c_S,nvH_S^{-1})$.
  179  \end{theorem}
  180  \begin{proof}
  181  Write $s=\sy$ and $b=b_0s^2$. By \eqref{eq:UX}, $z^c_S=X_S\tr UU\tr y^r=X_S\tr Cy^r=s\,X_S\tr y=s\,z_S$ and $\yc\tr\yc=s^2y\tr y$, hence $Q^c_S=s^2Q_S$.
  182  
  183  \emph{The v3 joint posterior.} The working model of \texttt{STATEMENT.md} \S1 has, at the observed $y$, the unnormalised joint posterior density
  184  \[
  185  p(S,\beta,\sigma^2)=\vp(S)\,\N_n(y;X_S\beta,\sigma^2I_n)\,\N_k\big(\beta;0,n\sigma^2(G_S+I)^{-1}\big)\IG(\sigma^2;a_0,b_0),
  186  \]
  187  with respect to counting measure on $\Om$ times Lebesgue measure on $\R^S\times(0,\infty)$. Its total mass is $\sum_\Om\vp(S)m(S)=Z\in(0,\infty)$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:closed}. Its $S$-marginal is $\pi$.
  188  
  189  \emph{Change of variables.} The map $(\beta,\sigma^2)\mapsto(\theta,v)=(s\beta,s^2\sigma^2)$ is a linear bijection of $\R^S\times(0,\infty)$ with inverse Jacobian determinant $s^{-k-2}$. So the image law has unnormalised density $q(S,\theta,v)=p(S,\theta/s,v/s^2)\,s^{-k-2}$. We evaluate the three factors. By \eqref{eq:UX}, $y-X_S\theta/s=U(\yc-X_{c,S}\theta)/s$ and $U$ is an isometry, so
  190  \[
  191  \N_n(y;X_S\theta/s,(v/s^2)I_n)=s^{n}(2\pi v)^{-n/2}\exp\Big\{-\frac{\|\yc-X_{c,S}\theta\|^2}{2v}\Big\}.
  192  \]
  193  Next, $\N_k(\theta/s;0,n(v/s^2)(G_S+I)^{-1})=s^k\N_k(\theta;0,nv(G_S+I)^{-1})$. Finally,
  194  \[
  195  \IG(v/s^2;a_0,b_0)=\frac{b_0^{a_0}}{\Gamma(a_0)}\Big(\frac v{s^2}\Big)^{-a_0-1}e^{-b_0s^2/v}=s^2\,\IG(v;a_0,b_0s^2).
  196  \]
  197  Hence $q(S,\theta,v)=\vp(S)s^n(2\pi v)^{-n/2}e^{-\|\yc-X_{c,S}\theta\|^2/(2v)}\N_k(\theta;0,nv(G_S+I)^{-1})\IG(v;a_0,b)$. Now
  198  \[
  199  (2\pi v)^{-n/2}\IG(v;a_0,b)=(2\pi v)^{-(n-1)/2}(2\pi)^{-1/2}\frac{b^{a_0}}{\Gamma(a_0)}v^{-a_0-3/2}e^{-b/v}
  200  \]\[
  201  =(2\pi v)^{-(n-1)/2}\frac{\Gamma(0.51)\,b^{a_0-0.51}}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\Gamma(a_0)}\IG(v;0.51,b),
  202  \]
  203  and $b^{a_0-0.51}=(b_0s^2)^{-1/2}=b_0^{-1/2}s^{-1}$. Therefore
  204  \begin{equation}\label{eq:q}
  205  q(S,\theta,v)=c_n(s)\,\vp(S)\,g_{S,b}(\theta,v),\qquad c_n(s)=\frac{s^{n-1}\Gamma(0.51)}{\sqrt{2\pi b_0}\,\Gamma(0.01)} .
  206  \end{equation}
  207  
  208  \emph{Conclusions.} The change of variables preserves integrals. Integrating \eqref{eq:q} over $(\theta,v)$ gives $\vp(S)m(S)=c_n(s)\vp(S)m^c_b(S)$, so $m(S)=c_n(s)m^c_b(S)$ for all $S\in\Om$. Summing gives $Z=c_n(s)Z^c_b$. The normalised image law is $q/Z=\vp(S)g_{S,b}/Z^c_b$, the density of $\Pi_b$. The expressions for BF and $\pi$ follow because $c_n(s)$ does not depend on $S$. The conditionals are those of the contrast model at rate $b$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:closed}).
  209  \end{proof}
